# CallForges

> CallForges is a cloud phone system for sales and support teams: local numbers in the US, UK, Canada and Australia, a power and parallel dialer, AI call notes, an AI voice agent, two-way SMS, call routing and CRM call logging. Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial.

The app is at https://app.callforges.com (sign up at https://app.callforges.com/signup). Plans and prices: https://callforges.com/pricing.html. Help center: https://callforges.com/help. The full text of this site: https://callforges.com/llms-full.txt. AI tools can connect to a CallForges workspace through its MCP server: https://callforges.com/for-agents.html.

This file holds the text of the website and the help center. The blog posts are listed, with links, in https://callforges.com/llms.txt.

URL: https://callforges.com/

# Call like a local.

Local US, UK and Australian numbers, an auto dialer, and an AI agent that picks up 24/7.

14-day trial · 50 min inbound + 50 min outbound · No card required

## Everything a call needs.

### Local wherever you sell.

US, UK, Canada and AU numbers in a minute, plus 50+ more countries. Port yours, hassle-free, even during your trial.

### Your name, not Spam Likely.

Register your business once in the Compliance center. Your US calls go out verified, show your company name, and your numbers are registered so they are less likely to be labeled spam. Free, even during your trial.

### Talk more. Dial less.

One contact after another. Voicemails dropped for you.

### Calls, written down.

An AI summary of the call, synced to your CRM.

### Never miss a call.

Picks up at midnight. Answers from your docs and books the callback for morning.

### The right team, first ring.

Route by country, time zone or VIP status.

### Text from the same number.

Two-way SMS from your numbers, in one shared Inbox. Assign, schedule and follow up.

## One team. Every time zone.

Your morning call block starts here.

Three examples. CallForges follows every contact's local time, wherever they are.

## Start at $15 a seat.

No seat minimum. Set your team size and see what you'd pay.

Per month, billed annually. CallForges transcription is billed per minute and not included. Aircall list prices, Sept 2026.

### Keep your numbers. We port them, hassle-free.

## Questions.

### Do I need new hardware?

No. CallForges runs on desktop, web, iOS and Android.

### Can I keep my numbers?

Yes. We handle the port for you, hassle-free, and your old system keeps working until the move completes. Porting a US number costs $10, and you can start during your free trial.

### Will callers know it's AI?

Yes. The agent introduces itself as a virtual assistant and hands off to a person on request.

### Can I send SMS?

Yes. Send and receive SMS from your numbers in a shared Inbox, billed per message from your credits. US numbers register with the carriers first (A2P 10DLC).

### Will my calls show as Spam Likely?

We help prevent it. Register your business once in the Compliance center: your US calls go out verified (SHAKEN/STIR), your company name shows as caller ID, and your numbers are registered so they are less likely to be labeled spam. Registration is free, even during your trial. See what is included

### What does international cost?

100 to 1,000 free minutes per user each month for calls to and from the US, UK, Australia and Canada (inbound and outbound), depending on your plan. After that, per minute, and each call's cost shows in Billing after the call. Fair usage policy

## Your next customer is in another time zone.

No card required · Cancel anytime

# Dial less. Talk more.

CallForges rings your list from a local number, inside each contact's working hours. Call one contact after another, or several at once, and the next call is already ringing when you hang up.

14-day free trial · No card to start Campaigns start with your plan, from $15 per user a month, billed annually

## Pick the pace for the list.

### Hang up. It's ringing.

The next contact rings as soon as the last call ends. Voicemail? Drop your recording in one click and keep going.

Best for outreach blocks, event follow-ups and big lists.

### Ring several. Talk to one.

The dialer rings several contacts at the same time and connects you to the first person who answers.

Best for large lists where most calls go unanswered.

## Everything the dialer needs.

### Local, verified caller ID

Ring from a number in the contact's own country. US calls go out verified and show your company name once your business is registered.

### Calling windows

Only dials inside each contact's working day.

### Voicemail drop

Record it once. Drop it in one click.

### Retry rules

Missed contacts come back on a schedule.

### AI summaries

A short summary of the call, synced to your CRM.

### Recording and coaching

Every call recorded. Scorecards and wallboards on Scale.

## Your CRM stays the record.

Calls, outcomes and AI summaries land on the right contact, so reps never copy notes between tabs.

Coming from another dialer? Import your lists from CSV or your CRM. We port your numbers for you, including during the trial; a US number costs $10 to port.

## Dialer questions.

### What is an auto dialer?

An auto dialer calls the numbers on your list for you. In CallForges, a rep starts a session and the dialer rings each contact in turn. When the call ends, the rep logs the outcome and the next contact rings.

### What's the difference between power and parallel dialing?

Power dialing rings one contact at a time and calls the next as soon as the last call ends. Parallel dialing rings several contacts at once and connects you to the first person who answers.

### Which plans include the auto dialer?

Every paid plan: Starter ($15 per user per month, billed annually, or $19 monthly), Business ($29 annually, $39 monthly) and Scale ($45 annually, $59 monthly). Scale adds dialer campaigns with custom retry rules. The free trial covers calls and numbers; campaigns start with your plan.

### Do dialer calls use my free minutes?

Yes. Auto dialer calls use minutes the same way as manual calls: calls to and from the US, Canada, UK and Australia use your plan's free minutes first, then bill per minute. See the fair usage policy.

### Who is responsible for calling rules and consent?

You are. Calling windows help you call inside working hours, but consent, calling-hour and do-not-call rules differ by country, and following them is your responsibility under our Terms.

### Can I bring my numbers and lists?

Yes. Import lists from CSV or your CRM. We port your numbers for you, including during your free trial. Porting a US number costs $10.

## Your next fifty calls, without the clicking.

Load a list, pick power or parallel, and start talking. Free for 14 days, no card to start; campaigns start with your plan.

URL: https://callforges.com/ai-agent.html

# Every call answered. Even at 3am.

When your team logs off, the CallForges agent picks up. It answers from your own help docs, in the caller's language, and books the callback for the morning.

14-day free trial · No card to start 100 agent minutes per user on Business, then $0.12 a minute

## Live in three steps.

### Add your docs

Help articles, policies, FAQs. The agent answers from these and nothing else.

### Choose when it answers

Send calls to it after hours, on weekends, or whenever your routing says.

### Turn it on

Pick the number. Calls start getting answered tonight.

## It never pretends to be a person.

- Every call starts by saying it's an automated assistant.

- Callers can reach a person or leave a message at any point.

- It only answers from the sources you give it.

## Pay for the minutes it talks.

Agent minutes are separate from calling minutes and pooled across your account.

After a transfer to your team, the rest of the call uses normal calling minutes. Extra agent minutes are $0.12 each.

## Agent questions.

### What is an AI voice agent?

It's an assistant that answers your phone line in a natural voice. It talks with the caller, answers from the documents you give it, and books a callback or hands the call to your team when a person is needed.

### When does it pick up?

You decide with call routing. Most teams send calls to the agent after hours, so nights and weekends are covered and your team keeps the day.

### What can it answer?

Questions covered by the help docs, policies and FAQs you give it, in 30+ languages. You own those sources, so keep them current. If it doesn't know, it books a callback instead of guessing.

### Will callers know it's AI?

Yes. The agent tells callers they're speaking with an automated assistant, and they can always ask for a person or leave a message.

### How is it billed?

Per minute the agent spends on the call, at $0.12. Business includes 100 agent minutes per user each month and Scale includes 250, pooled across your account. Once a call is transferred to a person, the rest uses normal calling minutes.

## Tonight's calls, answered.

Add your help docs, pick your number, and let the agent take the night shift. Free for 14 days, no card to start.

Numbers in 56 countries and territories, per user or shared by a team. Price depends on country and type. See all number prices

A free-to-call line for support desks. $5 in the US, Canada and UK, $25 in Australia, more in other countries.

Minutes the AI agent spends on calls beyond your plan's pool. Transfers to your team aren't counted.

Billed at the published rate for each destination and paid from your credits. No bundles to buy.

AI transcripts of your calls, billed per transcribed minute at the published rate.

Each SMS you send or receive, billed at the rate for the country it reaches and paid from your credits. US numbers register with the carriers first, who charge their own registration fees.

### Top up as you go

Credits pay only for calls and SMS: minutes beyond your pool, calls to and from other countries, SMS, call transcripts and AI call summaries. Top up at any time, including in the free trial.

## Pricing questions.

### Is there a seat minimum?

No. Start with one seat and add people when you need them.

### Can I mix plans across my team?

No. Your workspace has one plan and every user is on it, so a plan change applies to everyone.

### What do I get in the free trial?

14 days, and no card needed to start. You get a free local US, UK, Canada or Australia number, 50 inbound and 50 outbound minutes, and calls of up to 5 minutes each. You can take up to 5 numbers per workspace, paying for each one after the first on your card, and top up credits at any time. Adding a card removes the 5-minute limit. Campaigns (the power and parallel dialers) start with your plan. You can port your numbers during the trial. If you don't choose a plan, the trial number is released on a later date, shown on the Phone Numbers page.

### How are minutes counted?

Per minute, rounded up to the next full minute. Calls to and from the US, UK, Australia and Canada use your plan's free minutes first. See the fair usage policy for details.

### Do unused free minutes roll over?

No. Your free minutes reset at the start of each billing month.

### How is the AI voice agent billed?

Per minute the agent spends talking, at $0.12. Business and Scale include a pool of minutes each month. Time after a transfer to a person counts as a normal call.

### How do credits work?

Credits pay only for calls and SMS: minutes after your free pool, calls to and from other countries, call transcripts, AI call summaries and SMS. Your plan, seats, numbers and one-time fees such as porting or SMS registration go on your card. Anything you buy between invoices is charged at once. A number is charged its full monthly price when you buy it, your next invoice skips it, and it renews with your plan from the invoice after. You can top up credits at any time, including during the free trial.

### How is transcription billed?

Call transcription is billed per transcribed minute, at the published rate.

### How is SMS billed?

Each SMS you send or receive is billed per message, at the rate for the country it reaches, and paid from your credits. A long SMS goes out in parts, and each part counts as one. US numbers register with the carriers first, who charge their own registration fees.

### Can I port my numbers?

Yes, including during your free trial. Porting a US number costs $10. Fees for other countries vary by carrier.

### Are plan changes prorated?

Yes. An upgrade or an added seat is charged to your card at once, only for the rest of the current billing period, up to your renewal date. A downgrade starts at your renewal.

### Can I cancel?

Monthly plans cancel anytime. Annual plans can change or downgrade at renewal.

## Try Business free for 14 days.

No card required to start.

## Five reps, a power dialer and AI summaries.

Aircall and JustCall charge extra for the dialer and AI. Business includes both.

## Coming from another tool?

### Keep the power dialer. Drop the add-ons.

No three-seat minimum, no $9 per-user AI add-on (transcripts are billed per minute), and AI agent minutes at a quarter of the pay-as-you-go rate. Port your Aircall numbers and keep them live until the move completes.

### The same dialer workflow, with AI on the plan.

Power dialing and AI summaries both come with Business. Your lists and dispositions import from CSV or your CRM.

### When you outgrow texting in the US.

Quo is a good fit for small teams talking to US customers. When you need an auto dialer and cheaper calls outside North America, CallForges covers both.

### Dialpad-level AI, plus the dialer.

Dialpad's AI is strong. CallForges adds the auto dialer to the core plan and includes up to 1,000 free minutes a month with simple per-minute rates after that.

# CallForges for AI agents

Last updated: 28 November 2026

Two things live here. AI assistants can read about CallForges as plain text. And you can connect your own AI tool to your CallForges workspace, so it can look things up and do work for you.

## 1. Read about CallForges

These files describe this website for AI assistants and agents. Use them to answer questions about what CallForges does, its plans and how to set it up.

- llms.txt: a short index of every page on this site, with one line on each.

- llms-full.txt: the text of the website and the help center in one plain-text file. Blog posts are listed in llms.txt.

- sitemap.xml: every page on this site, for search engines and crawlers.

Prices and plans are on the pricing page. Step-by-step guides are in the help center.

## 2. Connect an AI tool to your workspace

CallForges has an MCP server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard AI tools use to connect to apps. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or any other MCP client, then ask it about your calls, contacts, campaigns and texts, or have it do the work.

- Server URL `https://api.callforges.com/mcp` For Claude.ai, ChatGPT and other apps that sign in.

- Key URL `https://api.callforges.com/mcp/key` For a key, in Cursor, VS Code or Claude Code.

You'll find both in the app under Settings → MCP access. You need the "Connect AI tools (MCP)" permission, which an owner or admin gives in Settings → Roles & permissions.

## 3. Apps that sign in

Claude.ai and ChatGPT sign in with your CallForges account, so they need no key.

- In Claude.ai or ChatGPT, add a custom connector.

- Paste the Server URL: `https://api.callforges.com/mcp`

- Sign in with CallForges and pick your workspace.

The app then shows under Connected apps in Settings → MCP access. Click Disconnect to cut it off.

## 4. Tools that use a key

- In CallForges, open Settings → MCP access and click Create key.

- Name it, pick Read only or Read & write, and choose when it expires.

- Copy the key at once: you won't see it again. The app shows a ready-to-paste setup for Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code.

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add --transport http callforges https://api.callforges.com/mcp/key --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY"
```

### Cursor (~/.cursor/mcp.json)

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "callforges": {
      "url": "https://api.callforges.com/mcp/key",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code (.vscode/mcp.json)

```
{
  "servers": {
    "callforges": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.callforges.com/mcp/key",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

Click Revoke next to a key to stop it at any time.

## 5. What an AI tool can do

- Read only: your calls and their transcripts, contacts, lists, campaigns and their results, phone numbers, call workflows, texts, CRM connections, and your credits, plan and invoices.

- Read & write can also create and edit contacts, lists and campaigns, draft and publish call workflows, send texts and work your Inbox, log past calls to your CRM and import contacts from it.

- Only in the app: starting, pausing and stopping a campaign, placing calls, buying or releasing numbers, billing changes, and inviting users or changing roles.

## 6. You stay in control

- An AI tool works as you. It sees and does only what your role allows, and a change to your role applies to it at once.

- CallForges asks the tool to show you a text and get your yes before sending it, and to ask you before it publishes a workflow.

- Every change an AI tool makes is recorded in Settings → Activity with an MCP badge and the tool's name.

- Revoke a key or disconnect an app in Settings → MCP access, and it stops working on its next request.

Questions? Ask in the help center or write to hello@callforges.com.

# Security

Last updated: 8 November 2026

This page explains how CallForges protects your account, your calls and the data we exchange with the tools you connect, such as Clio. For what we collect and why, see our Privacy Policy.

## 1. Where your data is

Our application and database servers are in the United States. Our databases are not reachable from the internet: only our web server accepts outside connections.

## 2. Encryption

- All traffic to our website, app and API uses HTTPS (TLS).

- Data is encrypted at rest, including our databases and stored recordings.

- Access to the CRMs you connect is stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM.

## 3. Sign-in and passwords

- You can sign in with Google instead of a password.

- Passwords are stored only as Argon2 hashes, never in plain text.

- A new password is checked against known breached passwords. Only the first five characters of its hash leave our servers.

- Repeated failed sign-ins are rate limited and lock the account for a while.

## 4. Access control

- You decide who can do what in your workspace with roles and permissions. Only owners and admins can connect, change or disconnect an integration.

- Our internal admin console requires a password and an authenticator code.

## 5. Connected CRMs

- You connect a CRM through its own sign-in page. We never see or store your CRM password.

- We ask only for the permissions our features use, and use them only for those features, such as logging your calls.

- When you disconnect Clio, we revoke our access at Clio, delete our access tokens and remove the Clio names we held for that connection. Nothing in your Clio account is deleted.

## 6. Recordings and AI

- You choose, for each phone number, whether calls are recorded and transcribed.

- Recordings are kept in private storage. By default, a recording can't be shared outside CallForges, and inside it only members allowed to listen to calls can play it.

- Our AI subprocessors may use the data only to provide the feature to us and may not use it to train their own models.

## 7. How we build

- Every change is reviewed and must pass automated code analysis and tests before it is released.

- Database queries are parameterized, and every request is checked against your workspace and your permissions on the server.

## 8. Backups

We take a snapshot of our servers every day and keep each one for 7 days.

## 9. If something goes wrong

If a data breach is likely to affect you, we will notify you and the relevant regulators as the law requires.

## 10. Report a problem

If you find a security issue, write to support@callforges.com. Please give us a chance to fix it before telling anyone else.

URL: https://callforges.com/fair-usage.html

# Fair Usage Policy

Last updated: 10 October 2026

This Fair Usage Policy explains how calling minutes work on CallForges and what counts as normal business use. It forms part of our Terms and Conditions. If this policy and the Terms conflict, the Terms apply.

## 1. Included minutes

Every user licence includes free calling minutes each billing month for calls to and from phone numbers in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom and Australia:

- Free trial: 50 inbound and 50 outbound minutes. Each call can last up to 5 minutes until you add a card. You can take up to 5 numbers per workspace, paying for each one after the first on your card, and top up credits at any time.

- Starter: 100 minutes per user per month

- Business: 500 minutes per user per month

- Scale: 1,000 minutes per user per month

- The allowance is calculated at account level: your plan's minutes multiplied by the number of active paid users in that billing month.

- Inbound and outbound calls both use the allowance.

- Free minutes reset at the start of each billing month. Unused minutes do not roll over and have no cash value.

## 2. How we count minutes

- Calls are billed per minute. Any part of a minute is rounded up to the next full minute.

- Each connected call, including a call answered by voicemail, counts as at least 1 minute.

- Calls that do not connect (no answer, busy, invalid number) are not billed.

- Forwarded calls use minutes for each leg of the call.

## 3. After your free minutes

Once your account uses its monthly allowance, further calls to and from the US, Canada, UK and Australia are billed per minute at the rates published on our pricing page. Calls to every other country, and to premium-rate, special-service or satellite numbers, are always billed per minute and never use the free allowance. Each call's cost shows in Billing after the call.

Minutes beyond your allowance, calls to and from other countries, call transcripts, AI call summaries and SMS are paid from your credits. Number rent and one-time fees such as porting are charged to your card. You can top up credits at any time, including during the free trial.

## 4. AI agent and transcription minutes

AI voice agent minutes are separate from calling minutes. Business plans include 100 agent minutes per user per month and Scale plans include 250, calculated at account level. Additional agent minutes are billed per minute at the published rate. When the agent transfers a call to a person, the rest of the call uses normal calling minutes.

Call transcription is billed separately, per transcribed minute, at the published rate. Transcribed minutes do not use your calling allowance.

## 5. Normal business use

Minutes are included for the named user who holds the licence, making and receiving calls as part of their normal work: sales calls, follow-ups, customer support and similar conversations with real people.

## 6. What isn't allowed

The free allowance, and CallForges generally, may not be used for:

- Sharing one licence between several people, or rotating logins to spread usage.

- Reselling minutes or numbers, or connecting CallForges to another phone system, PBX, SIP trunk or call-center platform so that many people use one licence.

- Automated, machine-to-machine or pre-recorded calls without the consent the law requires.

- Traffic pumping, SIM boxing, call arbitrage, or calls made mainly to generate minutes or revenue.

- Calls that break the Acceptable Use rules in our Terms and Conditions.

## 7. Auto dialer use

Auto dialer calls use minutes the same way as manual calls. Because the dialer places calls quickly, we watch for patterns that suggest misuse, such as very short average call length, very high no-answer rates, or large numbers of calls to numbers on do-not-call registers. You are responsible for calling hours, consent and do-not-call rules in each country you call. See section 9 of the Terms and Conditions.

## 8. Monitoring and enforcement

We review usage to protect our network, our carriers and other customers. If we see usage that breaks this policy, we may, in this order where practical:

- Contact you to explain what we found and ask you to change it.

- Bill the affected minutes at our published per-minute rates.

- Limit calling volume, disable the auto dialer or pause specific numbers.

- Suspend or close the account, as described in our Terms and Conditions.

Where the law or a carrier requires us to act at once, for example to stop fraud or illegal calling, we may act without notice.

## 9. Changes

We may update this policy as our plans and carrier costs change. We will give at least 30 days' notice by email or in the app before a change that reduces your included minutes takes effect.

## 10. Contact

Questions about this policy: support@callforges.com

# Terms and Conditions

Last updated: 26 November 2026

These Terms and Conditions ("Terms") are an agreement between CallForges ("we", "us"), and the business or person that creates an account or uses our services ("Customer", "you"). By creating an account, starting a trial or using CallForges, you agree to these Terms, our Privacy Policy and our Fair Usage Policy. If you accept on behalf of a company, you confirm you are authorised to bind it.

## 1. The services

CallForges is a cloud-based business phone service. It includes inbound and outbound calling over the internet, local and toll-free phone numbers, a power and parallel auto dialer, call recording, AI transcription and summaries, an AI voice agent, call routing, and integrations with other software (together, the "Services"). You need a stable internet connection and a supported device to use the Services.

## 2. Emergency calls

CallForges is not a replacement for a traditional telephone line and does not support calls to emergency services, including 911 (US and Canada), 999 or 112 (UK) and 000 (Australia). You must keep another way to reach emergency services and tell your users about this limitation. We are not liable for any inability to reach emergency services through CallForges.

## 3. Accounts and users

- You must give accurate account and business information and keep it up to date.

- Each user licence is for one named person. Logins may not be shared.

- You are responsible for everything done under your account, and for keeping passwords and access secure. Tell us at once if you suspect unauthorised access.

- You must be at least 18 years old and use the Services for business purposes.

## 4. Phone numbers and porting

- We assign phone numbers to your account for your use. Numbers are regulated resources and you do not own them.

- Regulators in some countries, including the UK and Australia, require proof of name and address before a number can be assigned. You must provide this when asked, and we may withdraw a number if you do not.

- Porting in: we manage the porting process with your current carrier. Porting timelines depend on that carrier. Porting a US number costs $10; fees for other countries vary. You can port numbers during a free trial. You remain responsible for your contract with your previous provider.

- Porting out: you may move eligible numbers to another provider while your account is in good standing. Numbers in an unpaid or closed account may be released after 30 days.

- We may change or reclaim a number where a regulator or carrier requires it, or where it is used in breach of these Terms.

## 5. Plans, minutes and billing

- Subscriptions are charged per user licence, monthly or annually in advance, at the prices on our pricing page when you subscribe.

- Each user licence includes free minutes for calls to and from the US, Canada, UK and Australia: 100 per month on Starter, 500 on Business and 1,000 on Scale, and 50 inbound and 50 outbound minutes during a free trial, under our Fair Usage Policy.

- Usage beyond included allowances (calling minutes, AI voice agent minutes, call transcription, extra numbers and other add-ons) is billed per minute or per unit at published rates. Calls are billed per minute, rounded up to the next full minute.

- Credits: you can buy prepaid credits at any time, including during a free trial. Credits pay for calls beyond your free allowance, calls to and from other countries, call transcripts, AI call summaries and SMS. Seats, number rent and one-time fees such as porting or SMS registration are charged to your payment card.

- Upgrades and added seats are prorated: you pay only for the rest of the current billing period, up to your renewal date. Downgrades take effect at renewal.

- Prices exclude taxes and regulatory fees, which we add where required.

- Subscriptions renew automatically for the same term unless you cancel before the renewal date in your account settings.

- If a payment fails, we will tell you. If it is not paid within 14 days, we may suspend the Services until it is.

- Plan, seat and number rent charges are non-refundable, except where the law requires otherwise. If we charge you for something we then cannot provide, such as a phone number the carrier does not give us, a port that never receives a port date or an SMS registration the carrier never takes for review, we refund that charge to the card you paid with. We may also refund other amounts at our discretion. A refund of prepaid credits covers only credits not yet used, and those credits are removed from your account.

- We may change prices with at least 30 days' notice. Changes apply from your next renewal.

## 6. Free trials

Free trials run for 14 days unless we say otherwise, and we may extend a trial. During a trial you get one free local number in the US, UK, Canada or Australia, 50 inbound and 50 outbound minutes, and calls of up to 5 minutes each. A payment card is required for any number after the first, up to 5 numbers per workspace. Adding a card removes the 5-minute call limit. You can buy credits at any time. At the end of the trial, the account stops unless you choose a paid plan, and the trial number is released on a later date, shown on the Phone Numbers page. We do not charge you during a trial without your agreement.

## 7. Acceptable use

You must not use CallForges, or let others use it, to:

- Make calls or send messages that are unlawful, harassing, threatening, fraudulent or deceptive.

- Place unsolicited marketing calls, robocalls or pre-recorded calls without the consent the law requires.

- Display a caller ID you are not authorised to use, or hide or falsify caller ID to mislead the person called.

- Call numbers on do-not-call registers unless an exemption applies.

- Engage in traffic pumping, call arbitrage, reselling, or other uses described in the Fair Usage Policy.

- Upload malware, probe or disrupt our systems, or try to access other customers' data.

- Record, transcribe or analyse calls without the notice and consent the law requires.

- Infringe anyone's intellectual property or privacy rights.

## 8. Calling laws you must follow

You are responsible for making sure your calls, messages and recordings follow the laws of every country you call from and to. Depending on where you and your contacts are, these include:

- United States: the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), the Telemarketing Sales Rule, the National Do Not Call Registry, STIR/SHAKEN caller ID rules, and state telemarketing, calling-hours and recording laws.

- Canada: the CRTC Unsolicited Telecommunications Rules and the National Do Not Call List.

- United Kingdom: the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR), the Telephone Preference Service and Corporate TPS, UK GDPR, and Ofcom's rules on persistent misuse, including abandoned and silent calls.

- Australia: the Do Not Call Register Act 2006, the Telecommunications (Telemarketing and Research Calls) Industry Standard, the Spam Act 2003 and state surveillance and listening-device laws.

We may provide tools that help, such as calling-hour limits, do-not-call list uploads and recording announcements. Using those tools does not make us responsible for your compliance.

## 9. Auto dialer

The CallForges auto dialer has two modes: power mode calls one contact at a time, and parallel mode calls several contacts at once. When you use it, you must:

- Have the consent or lawful basis required to call each contact on your lists.

- Screen lists against the do-not-call registers that apply, and honour opt-out requests promptly.

- Set calling hours that match each contact's local time and the rules of their country or state.

- Connect every answered call to a live person or a lawful recorded message, and keep abandoned and silent calls within legal limits.

We may limit or disable the dialer on an account if its usage suggests a breach of these Terms or of calling laws.

## 10. Call recording and transcription

Recording and transcription laws differ by country and, in the US and Australia, by state. Some require every party on the call to consent. You decide whether to record and transcribe calls, and you are responsible for giving any required notice (for example, an announcement at the start of the call) and obtaining any required consent. You can turn recording and transcription on or off for users, numbers and teams. Transcription is billed per transcribed minute at the published rate.

## 11. AI features

- AI features, including transcription, summaries, action items, coaching and the AI voice agent, are generated automatically and may be incomplete or wrong. Review important outputs before you rely on them.

- The AI voice agent must tell callers they are speaking with an automated assistant, and callers must be able to reach a person or leave a message. You must not configure the agent to pretend to be human.

- You are responsible for the instructions, knowledge sources and documents you give the AI voice agent, and for the answers it gives from them.

- Do not use AI features to make decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on a person without human review.

- We use carefully selected third-party AI providers to process call audio and text. They process your data only to provide the feature to you and are not allowed to use it to train their own models.

- We do not use your call recordings or transcripts to train AI models without your written consent. We may use aggregated, de-identified usage data to improve the Services.

## 12. Your data

You own the data you and your users put into CallForges, including contacts, call recordings, voicemails, transcripts and AI outputs ("Customer Data"). You give us permission to host, process and transmit Customer Data only as needed to provide, secure and support the Services. For Customer Data we act as your processor, and our Privacy Policy and Data Processing Addendum (available on request) apply. You can export Customer Data while your account is active and for 30 days after it closes, after which we delete it as described in our Privacy Policy.

## 13. Third-party integrations

If you connect CallForges to other services, such as a CRM, calendar or messaging tool, your use of those services is governed by their terms. You authorise us to exchange data with them as needed for the integration. We are not responsible for third-party services or changes they make.

## 14. Intellectual property

You must not copy, resell, reverse engineer or build a competing product from the Services. If you send us feedback, we may use it without obligation to you.

If we remove a major feature you pay for, we will give reasonable notice.

# Privacy Policy

Last updated: 6 November 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how CallForges ("we", "us") collects, uses and protects personal information when you visit our website, create an account, or use our cloud phone, auto dialer and AI services. It also explains the rights you have and how to use them.

## 1. Our role

- Controller: for information about our website visitors, account holders and billing contacts, we decide how the information is used.

- Processor: for information our customers put into CallForges, such as contact lists, call recordings, voicemails, transcripts and AI summaries ("Customer Data"), we process it on the customer's instructions. The customer (usually your employer, or the business that called you) is the controller and is responsible for telling you how it uses your information.

## 2. Information we collect

- Account information: name, work email, phone number, company, job role and login details.

- Billing information: billing contact, address and transaction records. Card details are handled by our payment provider; we do not store full card numbers.

- Number registration information: business name, address and proof of identity where regulators require it to assign phone numbers, for example in the UK and Australia.

- Call and usage records: numbers called and calling, time, duration, call outcome, cost, IP address and device information.

- Call content (Customer Data): recordings, voicemails, transcripts, AI summaries and AI voice agent conversations, only where our customer turns these features on.

- Contact data (Customer Data): names, numbers, time zones and notes that customers upload or sync from their CRM.

- Website and app data: pages visited, features used, browser type and cookie identifiers.

- Support and communications: messages, emails and calls with our team.

## 3. How we use it

- To provide the Services: connect and route calls, run the auto dialer, record and transcribe calls, and deliver AI features the customer has enabled.

- To assign and manage phone numbers and meet telecom regulatory duties.

- To bill you, including counting minutes under our Fair Usage Policy.

- To detect and prevent fraud, illegal calling and abuse of our network.

- To provide support and send service messages, such as security alerts and billing notices.

- To improve the Services using aggregated or de-identified usage data.

- To send product news and offers, where the law allows. You can opt out at any time.

- To comply with the law and respond to lawful requests.

## 4. Legal bases (UK and EU)

Where UK or EU data protection law applies, we rely on: performance of our contract with you; our legitimate interests in running, securing and improving our business (balanced against your rights); compliance with legal obligations, including telecom and tax rules; and your consent where the law requires it, for example for some cookies and marketing.

## 5. AI processing

- When a customer turns on transcription, summaries, coaching or the AI voice agent, call audio and text are processed by our systems and by carefully selected AI subprocessors to produce those outputs.

- Our AI subprocessors may use the data only to provide the feature to us and may not use it to train their own models.

- We do not use call recordings or transcripts to train AI models without the customer's written consent.

- The AI voice agent tells callers it is an automated assistant. AI outputs are not used to make decisions with legal or similarly significant effects about you.

## 6. Who we share it with

We do not sell personal information and do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. We share it only with:

- Telecom carriers and number providers that connect calls and host phone numbers.

- Service providers for cloud hosting, speech-to-text and AI, payments, email, customer support and analytics, under contracts that restrict their use of the data. A current list of subprocessors is available on request.

- Integrations you connect, such as your CRM, when you or your administrator enable them.

- Authorities where the law requires it, for example lawful interception or disclosure requests, or to protect rights and safety.

- A buyer or successor if we are involved in a merger, acquisition or sale of assets, subject to this policy.

## 7. International transfers

CallForges serves customers in several countries, so information may be processed outside the country where it was collected, including in the United States, where our servers are. Where UK or EU law applies, we protect transfers with approved safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and the UK International Data Transfer Addendum. For Australian personal information, we take reasonable steps to make sure overseas recipients handle it in line with the Australian Privacy Principles.

## 8. How long we keep it

- Call recordings, voicemails and transcripts: for the period the customer sets in their account, or until they delete them.

- Customer Data after an account closes: available for export for 30 days, then deleted from live systems within 90 days and from backups within a further 90 days.

- Call detail and billing records: for as long as tax, accounting and telecom laws require, typically up to 7 years.

- Marketing data: until you opt out or the information is no longer needed.

## 9. Security

We protect information with encryption in transit and at rest, access controls and least-privilege access for staff, multi-factor authentication for administrative access, logging and monitoring, and regular security reviews. Customers can control recording, retention and user permissions in their account. If a data breach is likely to affect you, we will notify you and the relevant regulators as the law requires.

## 10. Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete or export your personal information, to object to or restrict some processing, to withdraw consent, and to opt out of marketing.

- UK and EU: rights under the UK GDPR and EU GDPR, including the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (UK) or your local supervisory authority.

- United States: rights under state privacy laws such as the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA), including the right to know, delete and correct, and not to be discriminated against for using these rights.

- Australia: rights under the Privacy Act 1988 and the Australian Privacy Principles, including the right to complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) if you are not satisfied with our response.

- Canada: rights under PIPEDA and applicable provincial laws.

- India: rights under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, including grievance redressal through our Grievance Officer below.

To make a request, email privacy@callforges.com. We will verify your identity and respond within the time the law requires, usually within 30 days. If your request concerns Customer Data, we will pass it to the customer that controls it and help them respond.

## 11. If a CallForges customer called you

Businesses use CallForges to call their contacts. If a business called you using CallForges, that business decides why and how your information is used, including whether calls are recorded. Please contact that business first. To stop receiving their calls, ask them directly or use the do-not-call register in your country. If you think a CallForges customer is misusing our service, tell us at abuse@callforges.com and we will investigate.

## 12. Cookies

We use essential cookies to run our website and app, and, with your consent where required, analytics cookies to understand how our website is used. You can change your choices in your browser or in our cookie settings. We do not use advertising cookies in the CallForges app.

## 13. Children

CallForges is a business service and is not intended for anyone under 18. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

## 14. Changes

We may update this policy. We will post the new version here with a new date, and tell account owners by email or in the app about material changes.

## 15. Contact

CallForges Privacy questions and requests: privacy@callforges.com Grievance Officer / Data Protection Officer: Sonali Gupta, sonali.gupta@callforges.com

# Start your free trial

Every new workspace starts with a 14-day free trial with Business features. You don't need a card to start. Add one at any time to lift the trial's limits, or choose a plan straight away.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Create your account

- On callforges.com, click Start Free Trial. If you're on the sign-in page, click Create an account.

- Fill in First name, Last name, Work email, Username, Password and Workspace name. The workspace is where your team, numbers and calls live, so most people use their company name.

- Click Create account.

- On Check your email, type the code we sent you and click Verify and create account. If it hasn't arrived, click Resend code.

Fill in your details (step 2), then click Create account (step 3).

You can also click Continue with Google at the top of the form. CallForges then opens your new workspace, and you are its Owner.

Use your work email. A personal email address is refused with "Use your work email — this address can't be used to sign up."

## What the trial includes

- 14 days with Business features, counted from the day you create the workspace.

- One free local number in the US, the UK, Canada or Australia. You pick it yourself: see Buy a phone number.

- 50 outbound and 50 inbound minutes. They are counted separately, so when one runs out, the other keeps working.

- Calls of up to 5 minutes each. In the last minute, the call timer counts down.

- Calls to and from the US, Canada, the UK and Australia.

- Transcripts of calls on your trial minutes, with nothing deducted from your credits.

- Adding credits at any time, with or without a card.

- Up to 5 numbers. Each number after the first is paid by card when you buy it.

- Registering US numbers for SMS. The carriers' fees are paid by card when you submit: see Registration fees.

### What waits for a card or a plan

- Inviting teammates. The invite dialog says Upgrade to invite teammates.

- Calls to other countries and calls longer than 5 minutes.

- Incoming calls the trial can't cover, such as callers from other countries or with a hidden number. They aren't put through, and Call History marks them Blocked during your trial.

- Campaigns. The Campaigns page says Campaigns start with your plan. They turn on when your plan starts.

## Add a card to lift the limits

Owners and admins can do this.

- Open Billing in the sidebar. On Overview, the Plan details card shows Free trial and the days left.

- Click Add a card.

- In Choose your plan, pick Monthly or Annually and the plan your workspace moves to when the trial ends. Click Continue.

- Fill in your billing details and click Continue.

- Click Save card and enter your card on the payment page.

Billing → Overview: Plan details shows Free trial and the days left (step 1). Click Add a card (step 2).

We check your card with a small authorisation that is refunded at once. The trial's limits lift as soon as the card is saved: no 5-minute limit, calls to any country and invites. Calls beyond the trial minutes, and calls to other countries, are paid from credits.

Your plan starts when the trial ends, and your card is charged then. Until that day, the banner reads "Your plan starts on" with the date.

## Start your plan now

To end the trial early and start paying today, click Subscribe now in Plan details. You can also open Billing → Pricing and click Choose Starter, Choose Business or Choose Scale. The last step shows the Amount due today. Click Confirm and pay. See Plans and seats for how plans and seats are charged.

## See what's left

- The banner at the top of every page shows the days left in your trial.

- Billing → Usage balance shows your outbound and inbound trial minutes and how many you've used.

- For a quick look, click Credits in the sidebar, then View usage balance.

The banner shows the days left in your trial (1). Billing → Usage balance shows your outbound and inbound trial minutes (2).

## When the trial ends

- With a card: your plan starts, your card is charged for your seats, and campaigns turn on. If the charge doesn't go through, the invoice waits on Billing → Invoices with Pay now.

- Without a plan: the banner says "Your trial has ended — choose a plan to keep using CallForges." Calls and campaigns are paused and incoming calls aren't put through. You can still sign in, and your contacts and call history are kept. Owners and admins land on Billing → Pricing to choose a plan.

- Your numbers: Phone Numbers shows the date they will be released. Choose a plan before then to keep them.

# Make your first call

CallForges calls from your browser, so all you need is a number, a microphone and a few clicks. This guide walks you through your first call. For everything else the dialer does, see Place a call from the dialer.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- A number to call from. Your trial includes one free local number in the US, the UK, Canada or Australia. If Phone Numbers says No phone numbers yet, get one first.

- A microphone or a headset. A headset gives the other person the clearest sound.

- A browser that may use your microphone. It asks the first time you call.

## Get your number

Owners and admins can buy numbers. If you have the Member role, ask one of them to buy a number and make you its owner.

- Click Phone Numbers in the sidebar, then Add Number.

- In Number details, choose the Country and the Number type, pick a number from the list and click Save & Next.

- In Confirm details, check that the Owner is you, then click Confirm & Purchase.

Phone Numbers: click Add Number (step 1).

Your first local number in the trial is free. The full steps are in Buy a phone number.

## Place the call

- Click Dial at the top of any page. The dialer opens on the Phone tab.

- Choose the country from the dial code list, then type the number in Enter number. If the digits don't fit that country, the dialer tells you.

- Under Call via, choose the number the other person will see.

- Click Call.

- The first time, your browser asks to use your microphone. Click Allow.

Click Dial (step 1), type the number (step 2), choose your number under Call via (step 3), then click Call (step 4).

## On the call

The dialer shows Ringing, then Connected with a timer once they answer. While you talk you can use:

- Mute to turn your microphone off and on.

- Hold to put them on hold, and Resume to bring them back.

- Keypad to press digits, for example to get through a phone menu.

- Note to type notes about the call.

- Transfer to pass the call on: see Transfer a call.

On the call: Connected with its timer (1), and the Keypad, Note, Mute and Hold tiles (2).

Click End to hang up.

Until you add a card, each trial call can last up to 5 minutes. The timer counts down the last minute, and the call ends at the limit. To remove it, see Add a card to lift the limits.

## After the call

- The Logs tab in the dialer lists your recent calls.

- Call Logs in the sidebar opens Call History, where every call is listed. Click a call to see its details.

- If your workspace has the post-call details form turned on, it opens when a connected call ends. Choose a Disposition and add any notes.

## If the call doesn't go through

What you see | What to do

No number is assigned to you | Ask an owner or admin to assign one to you in Phone Numbers.

Choose a number to call from first. | Pick a number under Call via.

Microphone is blocked for this site | Allow the microphone in your browser's site settings (the icon in the address bar), then call again.

During the trial you can call the US, Canada, the UK and Australia. | Call a number in one of those countries, or add a card to call anywhere.

Your trial's outbound minutes are used up. | Add a card or choose a plan in Billing.

Recharge credits to make this call. | Add credits: see Add credits.

This number is on your Do Not Call list. | Remove the number from the list if you're allowed to call it.
