URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/place-a-call

# Place a call from the dialer

The dialer is a small phone panel that opens on top of any page in CallForges. Use it to call a number or a contact by hand, from one of your own phone numbers, right in your browser.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- You need a number to call from: one assigned to you, shared with you, or assigned to a team you are on. If you have none, the dialer shows No number is assigned to you. Ask an owner or admin to assign one in Phone Numbers.

- Calls go through your browser, so allow CallForges to use your microphone when the browser asks. If you blocked it, allow it again from the site settings in the address bar.

## Open the dialer

- Click Dial in the header of any page. The dialer opens as a panel. Drag it by its background to move it.

- Use the tabs at the bottom: Phone for the keypad, Logs for your recent calls and Contacts to search your contacts.

- The badge at the top reads Available, and Live call while you are on a call. You can't close the panel during a call.

Click Dial (step 1). The Phone, Logs and Contacts tabs are at the bottom (step 2), and the badge at the top reads Available (step 3).

The call icon in Contacts, the Call button on a contact's page and Call back in Call Logs also open the dialer, with the number filled in.

## Dial a number or a contact

- On Phone, pick the country from the flag, then type the number in Enter number. You can also paste it. A pasted number that starts with a country code picks the country for you.

- Under Call via, choose the number the other person sees. Your own numbers come first. Other numbers in the workspace are greyed out and marked Not assigned to you.

- Click Call, or press Enter.

Type the number in Enter number (step 1), choose the number the other person sees under Call via (step 2), then click Call (step 3).

If the digits can't be a real number for the chosen country, the dialer asks you to check them before it lets you call.

To call a contact, open Contacts in the dialer and search. Click the phone icon next to a contact to call them now, or click their name to put their number on the keypad. In Logs, the Recent, Missed and Voicemail tabs list your calls. Click one to put that number on the keypad.

The keypad starts on your workspace's default country. An owner or admin sets it in Settings → Dialer settings → Call defaults → Default country.

## During the call

The panel shows Dialing, then Ringing, then Connected with a timer once the other person answers. The tiles do the rest:

Tile | What it does

Keypad | Sends digits, for example to get through a phone menu.

Note | A notepad for this call, kept in this browser. To save notes on the call record, use the post-call form.

Mute | Turns your microphone off. Press it again to turn it back on.

Hold | Puts the call on hold. Your microphone goes off and the other person hears your number's hold message, or hold music if the number has none. Press Resume to come back.

Record | Starts or pauses the recording. If your number records calls, the call starts with Recording showing. Press to pause (Recording paused) and press again to carry on.

Voicemail | When you reach a voicemail box, pick one of your recorded messages and click Drop voicemail. The message plays into the voicemail box and your side of the call ends.

Transfer | Hands the call to someone else. See Transfer a call.

The first time someone presses Record, CallForges asks the workspace to confirm that people you call are told they are recorded. An owner or admin clicks Confirm and record. You record voicemail messages in Settings → My voicemail → Voicemail drops.

On a free trial without a card, each call lasts up to 5 minutes. In the last minute the timer counts down. Add a card to remove the limit. See Pricing.

## End the call and log the outcome

- Click End. The panel shows how long the call lasted, then closes.

- If your workspace uses the post-call form, it opens. Choose a Disposition, add a Note and a Rating if you like, and, for a saved contact, tick Add to Do Not Call list if they asked not to be called again.

- Click Save. Skip closes the form without saving.

The post-call form: choose a Disposition (step 2), then click Save (step 3).

If the form shows Disposition required by your workspace settings, there is no Skip: choose a disposition to close it. An owner or admin turns these on in Settings → Dialer settings → Call experience, with Post-call details form and Make call disposition mandatory to log calls.

## When a call is not placed

If a call can't go through, nothing is dialed and you see why:

- This number is on your Do Not Call list. Remove the number from the list if you are allowed to call it.

- You're out of credits or Your trial minutes are used up. Add credits or choose a plan in Billing. See Pricing.

- This workspace is suspended for non-payment. The amount due must be paid in Billing before calls start again.

- Not available on your workspace. The dialer is switched off for your workspace. Contact support.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/transfer-a-call

# Transfer a call

Transfer hands a live call to someone else. Transfer now passes the call over straight away. Ask first puts your caller on hold while you talk to the other person, then you decide what happens.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- You can transfer a connected call that is yours: a call you placed from the dialer, an incoming call you answered, or a power or parallel campaign call.

- The Transfer tile is greyed while the call is still ringing, while it is on its way to a voicemail drop, and after the call has already been transferred.

- A call a teammate transferred to you can't be transferred again from your side.

## Choose who gets the call

- On the live call, click Transfer. The Transfer call panel opens.

- Pick a tab: Number: find a saved contact under Search contacts, or type any number under Or type a number.

- Teammate: choose a user in your workspace. Their browser rings. Teammates marked Not online or Not available can't be picked.

- Team: choose a team. CallForges calls the team's number, and that number's call routing decides who rings.

- If you like, write a line in Note for whoever picks this up. The note is saved on the call record.

- Click Transfer now or Ask first, as described below.

## Transfer now

Use this when you don't need to speak to the other person first.

- Click Transfer now.

- Your caller is connected to the person you chose, and your side of the call ends.

If nobody answers the transfer:

- On a call you placed, the call ends.

- On an incoming call, the call rings you once more with Transfer not answered — back to you. If you don't answer, the call ends.

Not sure the other person is free? Use Ask first. If they don't answer, your caller simply comes back to you.

## Ask first

- Click Ask first. Your caller is put on hold and CallForges calls the person you chose.

- The panel shows two lines. Transferring to reads Connecting…, then Ringing…, then On the line once they answer. Your caller reads On hold.

- Talk to the other person. Your caller can't hear you.

- Choose what happens next: Hand over: you leave the call and the two of them keep talking.

- Merge: all three of you are on one call. When you are done, click Hand over or End. The other two stay connected.

- Back to caller: talk to your caller again while the other person waits on hold. Back to transfer switches back.

- Cancel: the other person is dropped and your caller comes back to you. You can cancel while it is still ringing, but not after Merge.

If the other person doesn't pick up, the transfer is cancelled and your caller is taken off hold, back with you.

A recording that is running carries on through the transfer. Once the call has been transferred, the Record tile can't be changed.

## What your teammate sees

When you transfer to a teammate, their browser rings like an incoming call. The card reads Transfer from your name, for your caller, so they know who is handing over whom. When they accept, they are on the call with your caller, or with you first if you chose Ask first.

## If a transfer doesn't start

Nothing changes on the call and a message says why:

- … is not available right now. or … isn't online right now. The teammate is set to unavailable, is outside their working hours, or doesn't have CallForges open. Pick someone else.

- That number is already on this call — pick another. You entered the number you are already talking to.

- The carrier has not confirmed the call yet. Try again in a moment. The call has only just connected. Wait a second and try again.

Every transfer shows on the call's page in Call Logs. For the controls on a live call, see Place a call from the dialer.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/create-a-campaign

# Create a campaign

A campaign is a list of leads that CallForges dials for you, one after another. You choose how it dials, which number it calls from, who it calls and when.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- Your role needs Create and edit campaigns. Owners, admins and members have it by default.

- You need an active phone number. If you have none, the form shows You need an active phone number to place calls. with Get a number.

- Have your leads ready: a contact list in CallForges, or a CSV file with at least a phone number column.

## Create the campaign

- Open Campaigns and click Create campaign.

- The form opens as Untitled Campaign. Click the name at the top to rename it.

- Under Dialer Type, choose: Power Dialer: calls one lead at a time.

- Parallel Dialer: calls several leads at once and connects you to the first who answers. Then set Number of parallel calls, Re-dial cancelled leads and, if you like, a Voicemail drop to play when a voicemail box answers.

- Under Call Via, pick the number your leads see. Your own numbers are offered first.

- Set Cooldown duration between two calls, in seconds.

- Under Audience, add your leads (see below).

- Choose the options at the bottom (see below).

- Click Create Campaign.

The new campaign: Dialer Type (step 3), Call Via (step 4), Cooldown duration between two calls (step 5) and Create Campaign (step 8).

If something is missing, CallForges tells you what to add, such as a contact list or a valid calling window. The new campaign opens as a Draft. Nothing is dialed until you start it.

You can't change the dialer type after the campaign is created.

## Add your leads

Select a list uses a contact list you already have:

- Click Select a list.

- Open List and pick one. Each list shows how many contacts it holds. Choose Create new list to make one here.

Click Select a list (step 1), then open List and pick one (step 2). Each list shows how many contacts it holds.

Upload leads imports a CSV file:

- Click Upload leads and choose your.csv file. CallForges detects the columns.

- Check how each column is mapped. Rows without a phone number are skipped. Existing contacts are matched by phone, then by email.

- Under Add to, choose New list and name it, or Existing list.

- Under Existing contacts, choose Update with CSV values or Keep as-is, only add to list.

- Click the Import button, which shows how many contacts it will import, then Done. That list is now the campaign's audience.

## Recording, Do Not Call and calling hours

- Enable default call recording for all calls in this campaign: records every connected call. It starts from your caller number's own recording setting.

- Respect Do-Not-Call (DNC) lists: contacts on your Do Not Call list are not dialed. Their status shows Do not call.

- Use the lead/contact's local time zone to call during their active hours: pick the Active Days, a Start Time and an End Time. These are the lead's own local hours.

When a lead's turn comes outside their hours, the lead is skipped and shows Out of timezone. It is not called again in this campaign. A lead with no time zone is always called. A US number uses its area code's time zone.

Start the campaign during your leads' hours, or many of them may be skipped as Out of timezone.

## Change the campaign later

On the campaign's page:

- Edit opens Edit campaign. Use Add a list or Pick contacts to add leads, and drag rows to change the dial order. Leads are dialed top to bottom. Click Save. A contact already in the campaign is not added twice.

- Settings opens Campaign settings: the name, the Caller number, Dialing behavior (Ring timeout, Wrap-up time, Cooldown between calls, Record calls, Skip Do-Not-Call contacts, and Auto-advance on a power campaign) and the Calling window. Click Save changes.

On the campaign's page: Edit (1) adds leads and changes the dial order; Settings (2) opens Campaign settings.

If the campaign is running, Edit and Settings first ask Pause campaign to edit?. The current call finishes, and nothing new is dialed until you resume. On a completed or ended campaign, Edit is read-only and Settings is greyed out.

## Call the same leads again

To call back leads from an earlier campaign, for example everyone who didn't answer:

- Open the campaign and tick the leads in its list. You can filter by status first.

- Click Create campaign. You can also use the ··· menu and Create campaign from leads….

- The form opens with a "follow-up" name, the same settings and the chosen contacts as the audience. Change anything you need and click Create Campaign.

Tick the leads you want to call again (step 1), then click Create campaign (step 2).

Next: Start, pause, resume or stop a campaign.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/start-pause-resume-stop

# Start, pause, resume or stop a campaign

You run a campaign from its page in Campaigns. Start it to begin dialing, pause it for a break, resume where it stopped, or stop it for good when you are done.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- Your role needs Run campaigns. Owners, admins and members have it by default. Without it, Start Campaign is greyed out.

- The campaign needs a caller number and leads. If one is missing, Start Campaign is greyed out and tells you what to add. The caller number is in Settings, the leads in Edit. See Create a campaign.

- Allow your browser to use the microphone. If it is blocked, you see Microphone needed.

- Keep the tab open while you dial. Closing or reloading the tab pauses a running campaign.

## Start a campaign

- Open the campaign. A new campaign shows READY.

- Click Start Campaign.

- On a power campaign, CallForges calls the first lead at the top of the dial order. The strip shows Power Dialing….

- When the lead answers, the strip shows Connected and the lead's contact page opens. The call has the same controls as the dialer: see Place a call from the dialer.

- When the call ends, you go back to the campaign and the strip shows Wrapping up… with a countdown to the next call (Next call in … secs). Its length comes from the campaign's wrap-up and cooldown settings.

A new campaign shows READY (step 1). Click Start Campaign (step 2).

During the countdown you can:

- Click the countdown (Skip Cooldown) to dial the next lead now.

- Click +10s to add 10 seconds.

- Click Log outcome to open the post-call form. While the form is open the countdown waits, and the strip reads Next call after you log the outcome.

If Auto-advance is off in the campaign's settings, click Dial next to place each call yourself.

A parallel campaign calls several leads at once and connects you to the first one who answers. Its strip shows each line as it rings.

When every lead has been called, the campaign becomes Completed. If the page says Nothing left to dial, click Close out to mark it completed.

## Pause a campaign

- Click Pause in the session strip.

- On a power campaign, a call that is already ringing or connected finishes normally. No new call is placed.

- On a parallel campaign with lines ringing, choose Pause now to hang up the ringing lines, or Pause after this round to let them finish (if someone answers, you are connected). Then click Pause.

Click Pause in the session strip (step 1).

Clicking Edit or Settings on a running campaign also pauses it, after you confirm Pause and edit.

CallForges pauses a campaign for you when:

- you close or reload the tab, or the campaign is left running with nobody dialing;

- the workspace runs out of credits. You see You're out of credits. Leads not called yet stay in the queue. See Pricing;

- the campaign's phone number is deleted. Attach a new one in Settings before you resume.

## Resume a campaign

- Open the campaign. It shows PAUSED.

- Click Resume. Dialing carries on from the next lead that has not been called.

A paused campaign shows PAUSED (step 1). Click Resume (step 2).

If the campaign shows NOT DIALING, it is still running but nobody is dialing it in this tab, for example after a reload. Click Resume dialing to pick up where it stopped.

If you are on another call, Resume waits and says Finish your other call first.

## Stop a campaign

- While you are dialing, click End session in the strip and confirm with End Campaign. A call in progress is hung up.

- When nobody is dialing, click Stop and confirm with Stop campaign.

When nobody is dialing, click Stop, then confirm with Stop campaign (step 2).

Either way the campaign becomes Ended. Leads not called yet are marked Skipped. An ended campaign can't be started again.

Only want a break? Use Pause, not Stop. To call the leads a stopped campaign never reached, create a follow-up campaign from them: see Call the same leads again.

## What each lead's status means

Each lead in the campaign's list shows a status. Pausing never changes it.

Status | Meaning

Pending | Waiting to be called.

Ringing | Being called now.

In progress | The lead answered and the call is live.

Completed | The lead answered and the call ended.

Voicemail | The call reached a voicemail box.

Voicemail dropped | A parallel campaign's voicemail drop played into the lead's voicemail box.

No answer | The phone rang and nobody picked up.

Busy | The line was busy.

Failed | The call could not be connected.

Cancelled | The call was cut off before the lead was reached, for example by Stop. On a parallel campaign, a lead waiting to be called again shows how many re-dials are left.

Cancelled by user | You hung up before the lead answered.

Skipped | Not called, for example because the campaign was stopped first or the lead had no number to call.

Do not call | The lead is on your Do Not Call list and the campaign respects it.

Out of timezone | The lead's turn came outside the campaign's calling hours in the lead's time zone. Not called in this campaign.

Insufficient credits | The call to this lead was not placed because of billing.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/how-the-parallel-dialer-works

# How the parallel dialer works

The parallel dialer rings several leads from a campaign at the same time and connects you to the first person who picks up. Use it on large lists where most calls go unanswered, so you spend your time talking instead of waiting.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- Campaigns, including the parallel dialer, start with your paid plan. During the free trial the Campaigns page reads Campaigns start with your plan. See pricing for the plans that include it.

- Users with the Owner, Admin or Member role can run a campaign. A custom role needs the permission to run campaigns.

- The campaign needs a phone number to call from and a list of leads. See Create a campaign.

- Allow your browser to use your microphone, and keep the CallForges tab open while you dial.

- One user runs a parallel campaign at a time.

## Set up a parallel campaign

- Open Campaigns and click Create campaign.

- Under Dialer Type, choose Parallel Dialer.

- In Number of parallel calls, choose how many leads ring at once.

- In Re-dial cancelled leads, choose how many times a lead the dialer cut is called again. Never is the default. See “Leads the dialer cuts” below.

- Optionally, pick a Voicemail drop. It plays when an answering machine picks up, then the dialer moves on.

- Under Call Via, pick the number to call from, and set the Cooldown duration between two calls.

- Add your leads and click Create Campaign.

Choose Parallel Dialer (step 2), then set Number of parallel calls (step 3), Re-dial cancelled leads (step 4) and, if you like, a Voicemail drop (step 5).

The voicemail drop plays only when Auto machine detection is on in Settings → Dialer settings. When it is off, an answering machine that picks up counts as an answer and is connected to you.

## What happens in each round

- On the campaign page, click Start Campaign. Your own line connects first, so the dialer only rings leads while you are ready to talk.

- The dialer rings the next leads on the list. The session bar shows how many lines are live, for example 3/3 lines, and the Active batch table under it shows each line and its status.

- When a line ends without an answer, the dialer rings the next lead in its place, so the batch stays full.

- The first person who answers is connected to you. The other lines are hung up at once: First pickup wins — other lines release automatically.

- The session bar reads Connected with a timer, and CallForges opens the lead's contact page.

The session bar shows how many lines are live, and the Active batch table shows each line and its status (step 2). First pickup wins (step 4).

## After each call

- When the call ends, the post-call form opens so you can log the outcome and notes. If it doesn't open, click Log outcome.

- The countdown shows Next call in N secs. Click it to Skip Cooldown, or click Extend for more time.

- The next round starts when the countdown ends and the post-call form is closed.

- When no leads are left, the session ends and the campaign is completed.

If your workspace runs out of credits, the campaign pauses after the current round. Lines already ringing finish, and you can still be connected to a lead who answers. Add credits, then click Resume. See Add credits.

## Leads the dialer cuts

The dialer hangs up a ringing lead, and marks it as cancelled, when:

- another lead answered first,

- the lead answered but nobody was free to take the call, or

- you chose Pause now while the line was ringing.

A cancelled lead goes back to the bottom of the list while it is within the Re-dial cancelled leads setting. With Never, it is not called again. Cancelled leads show as Cancelled on the campaign's leads table.

## Pause, resume and end

- Click Pause while lines are ringing, pick one of these, then click Pause again: Pause now: hang up the lines that are ringing.

- Pause after this round: let the ringing lines finish. If someone answers, you are connected. No new calls.

- Click Pause during a conversation and the campaign pauses without asking. Your call is never cut.

- Click Resume to start a new round.

- Click End session, then End Campaign, to stop. All ringing lines are hung up. An ended campaign can't be started again.

- If you close or reload the tab, the campaign pauses and ringing lines are hung up. Open the campaign and click Resume.

Click Pause while lines are ringing, then choose Pause now (1) or Pause after this round (2).

More detail is in Start, pause, resume or stop a campaign.

## Incoming calls during a session

You are never rung for an incoming call while your line is connecting, while leads are ringing, or while you are on a call. When the session is paused, in wrap-up or counting down, incoming calls ring you only if Allow incoming calls while busy is on in Settings → User settings. Answering one pauses your session.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/build-a-call-workflow

# Build a call workflow

A workflow decides what happens when someone calls one of your numbers: which hours count as open, who rings and in what order, and where the call goes when nobody answers. One workflow can serve many numbers, and each number runs exactly one workflow.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- Users with the Owner or Admin role can create, edit, publish and delete workflows. Members can view them.

- Every new or ported number starts on Direct line, the System default: it rings the number's owner and teams, then goes to voicemail. You only need a workflow when you want something different.

- To change the Direct line itself, open it from Workflows and click Duplicate it to make changes.

- If Workflows reads Not available on your workspace, contact support to turn it on.

## Create a workflow

- Open Workflows and click New workflow.

- Pick a template, or Start from scratch, and click Use template: Direct line: ring the number's owner, then take a voicemail.

- Business hours + voicemail: ring the owner Monday to Friday, 9 to 5. At any other time, take a voicemail.

- Business hours + forward: the same hours, then forward to a number you pick.

- Single-level IVR menu: callers press 1 or 2, and each key rings the owner, then takes a voicemail.

- Click the pencil next to the name to rename the workflow.

Pick a template, then click Use template (step 2).

## Add and set up steps

A workflow starts with the Incoming call trigger. Click + under a step to add the next one. The menu shows only the steps that fit there; click View more blocks for the rest. Click a step to open its settings on the right.

Click + under a step (1). The menu (2) shows the steps that fit there; View more blocks (3) shows the rest.

Step | What it does

Time rule | Sends calls down different paths by day and time, in the time zone you pick. Calls outside every slot take At any other time.

Date rule | Handles a holiday or other special date differently from Business days.

Ring users or teams | Rings the number's owner, chosen users or teams. It has an Answered and an Unanswered path.

Forward call | Sends the call to another phone number, such as a mobile or another office line. Enter it with its country code.

IVR menu | Plays a menu and sends the caller down a path for each key they press, with a No valid key path.

Extension message | Lets callers type a user's or team's extension to reach them directly.

Audio message | Plays a message, typed, uploaded or recorded, then continues.

Voicemail | Takes a message with the greeting and mailbox you choose.

Queue | Holds callers with music or a message while your users are busy, and connects them in order. It goes on a ring step's Unanswered path.

Post-call survey | After the call, asks the caller to rate it from 1 to 5 on their keypad.

A path with nothing after it ends the call. Click Add a note to leave a note for your team on the canvas. Use undo and redo if you change your mind.

## Choose who rings

- Click a Ring users or teams step.

- Under Ring to, choose Number owner, Users or Teams, and add the users or teams.

- Choose a Ringing order: Ring all (available users at once), Ring in order (top to bottom), Ring idle (whoever answered the fewest calls recently first) or Ring in round robin (starts after whoever answered last, so calls are shared evenly).

- For teams, each team also has its own ring order: Ring all users, Ring idle first or Ring in round robin.

- Set Ring for: how long each ring lasts before the next user or the Unanswered path.

A Ring users or teams step: Ring to (step 2), Ringing order (step 3) and Ring for (step 5).

CallForges skips users who aren't set to Available, are outside their working hours, are on a call or wrapping up, or don't have CallForges open. If nobody can take the call, it goes straight to the Unanswered path.

## Save and publish

- Save draft keeps your changes. A draft never takes calls.

- Click Publish to make it live. If something needs fixing, Can’t publish yet lists each problem with its step. The problems button in the top bar shows the same list.

- The status reads Draft, Published, or Published · unpublished changes when you have saved edits that aren't live yet.

- Calls already in progress keep the version they started on. New calls use what you just published.

Save draft (1) keeps your changes and Publish (2) makes them live. The status (3) reads Draft until you publish.

## Put numbers on the workflow

- In the workflow, click Numbers. It is available once the workflow is published.

- Pick the numbers and click Save numbers. A number already on another workflow moves to this one when you click Take off and save.

You can also start from the number: open Phone Numbers, click the number, open Call routing and click Change workflow, pick a published workflow and click Use workflow. Choose Direct line · System default to go back to the default. If you delete a workflow, its numbers move to the Direct line.

The Pause incoming calls switch under the workflow on Call routing stops the workflow from running: every incoming call on that number goes to voicemail until you turn it off.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/buy-a-phone-number

# Buy a phone number

Buy a number to call from and to take calls on. You pick the country, type and number, choose who owns it and who else can use it, then confirm. The number is ready to use as soon as the purchase goes through.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- Users with the Owner or Admin role can buy numbers.

- Every user gets one free local number in the US, UK, Canada or Australia. Extra numbers are billed monthly at the price for their country and type. See pricing.

- In the free trial, your trial includes one free number. You can buy more, each one paid by card when you buy it; the payment page takes a card if you haven't added one. The trial includes up to 5 numbers. Choose a plan to add more.

- A paid number is paid by card when it is bought, so it needs a user who manages billing. Otherwise the screen reads Ask an owner or admin who manages billing to buy it.

- If buying numbers reads Not available on your workspace, contact support.

## Choose a number

- Open Phone Numbers and click Add Number.

- On Number details, pick a Country.

- Pick a Number type: Local number, Mobile number or Toll-free number. Only the types sold in that country are shown.

- Narrow it down if you like: a State or province and an Area code, or a Toll-free prefix for a toll-free number.

- To find specific digits, type them in Search for a specific number and choose Contains, Starts with or Ends with.

- Check the Suggested number and its price. Click shuffle for another suggestion, or Choose a different number to browse the list.

- Click Save & Next.

Number details: pick a Country (step 2) and a Number type (step 3), check the Suggested number (step 6), then click Save & Next (step 7).

## Name it and choose who uses it

On Confirm details:

- Friendly name (optional): a label your team will recognise, like Boston Main.

- Owner (required): you own the numbers you buy unless you pick someone else.

- Share with users (optional): these users can call from this number. Incoming calls follow its call routing.

- Shared teams (optional): the members of these teams can call from it too, and the teams ring for its incoming calls by default.

Confirm details: Friendly name (1), Owner (2), Share with users (3) and Shared teams (4).

## Countries that ask for verification

Some countries ask who a number belongs to before it can be sold. For those, Confirm details shows Verification required:

- With no submission yet, click Start verification. You verify once per number type (local, mobile or toll-free), as a business or an individual, with a few details, a proof-of-identity document and an address. It covers every number of that type you buy in that country afterwards: mobile and local numbers are verified separately.

- While your submission is under review, you can save the number now. We buy it as soon as the verification is approved, and charge its first month then. Nothing is charged before that.

- With an approved submission, pick it under the verified submission field. If you have only one, it is picked for you.

## Buy it

- Check the Pricing line. A free number shows Included in your plan. A paid number shows its monthly price, and Due today is one month at the full monthly price.

- Click Confirm & Purchase for a free number. For a paid one, click Continue to payment, check Amount due today and Next charged on, then click Confirm and pay. Your saved card is charged at once; with no card saved, the payment page opens.

- You see Number purchased, and the number appears on Phone Numbers.

A paid number is charged its full monthly price when you buy it. Your next invoice skips it, and from the invoice after that it's charged with your plan. Nothing comes out of your credits.

If you see "Payment failed. Update your card.", the number wasn't purchased. Update your card in Billing, then buy the number again.

If you see The carrier did not accept this purchase, try again or pick another number. Your payment is kept for 24 hours for another number of the same kind. If you don't use it by then, it's refunded to your card.

## After you buy

- Click the number on Phone Numbers to open its settings: General, Call routing, Greetings, Recording & transcripts and Compliance.

- A new number starts on Direct line, the System default: it rings the number's owner and teams, then goes to voicemail. To change that, see Build a call workflow.

- The owner, its shared users and the members of its teams can call from it on the dialer. Campaigns call from the number picked on the campaign.

Already have a number with another provider? You can bring it with you instead. See Port your number to CallForges.

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/port-your-number

# Port your number to CallForges

Porting moves a number you already have with another provider into your CallForges workspace, so your customers keep calling the number they know. US local numbers go through a step-by-step wizard. Other countries and US toll-free numbers are ported on request by our porting team.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- Users with the Owner or Admin role can port numbers. Other users can see the requests on the Porting tab.

- You can port numbers during your free trial.

- If porting reads Not available on your workspace, contact support.

- Porting a US number costs $10 per number, paid when you submit the request: it is charged to your saved card, or the payment page opens if you have none. A number that ends without a confirmed port date (your provider rejects it, or the request is canceled before its date) is refunded to your card. Fees for other countries vary by carrier: our porting team sets the fee and you pay its invoice from Billing. See pricing.

- Have these ready: a recent invoice from your current provider, your carrier and address details, and the numbers with their port-out PINs, if your provider uses them.

- Important: don't cancel your current service until your number is fully ported. Doing so may cause delays or failure in the porting process.

## Port US local numbers

Open Phone Numbers and click Port number. The steps are listed on the left. Save and next saves each step to a draft, so you can leave and finish later.

- Number details: pick the Country and the Number type. Read Porting information & charges and click Next.

- Upload documents: pick your Current service provider and upload your most recent invoice from them, as a PDF, JPEG or PNG.

- Enter numbers: click Enter numbers manually and type each number, with its Port-out PIN (optional). Or upload a CSV file; click Download sample CSV to see the format. Each number is checked as you enter it, and any problem shows on its row.

- Application details: these details must match your invoice exactly. Fill in the Account type (Business or Individual), the name on the account, the Current provider account number, the Billing telephone number (optional), the Authorized representative, the Service address, and optionally a Preferred port date and notification e-mails.

- Confirm details: check each step, tick I’m authorized to move these numbers and the details match my carrier account. and click Submit request. The port fee is charged to your saved card and the request is sent. If the card is declined, the request says Awaiting payment and nothing is sent to your provider: update your card in Billing and it is charged again at once, or pay the open invoice in Billing → Invoices. If Confirm details says "The porting fee couldn’t be loaded, so the request can’t be submitted yet.", the fee couldn't be read just then: Submit request stays off and nothing is charged until you click Try again and the fee shows.

The authorized representative receives an e-mail with the authorization to sign. It comes from our carrier partner, so ask them to look out for it. The port can't go ahead until it is signed.

## Port other numbers on request

For any other country, or a US toll-free number, the Number details step says porting is available on request. A US number the check says must be moved by hand links to the same form.

- Click Submit request to open Request a port.

- Check the Country and Number type, and list the Numbers to port, one per line.

- Check the Contact email, add notes if you like, and attach an invoice, a signed authorization or a customer service record if you have them.

- Click Submit request. Our porting team will reach out to move these numbers for you.

Request a port: list the Numbers to port (step 2), check the Contact email and attach any files (step 3), then click Submit request (step 4).

## Track your request

Open Phone Numbers and the Porting tab. Click Continue on a draft to pick up where you left off, or View to open a request. The request page shows each step: Submitted, Waiting for signature, In progress, Port date set and Completed, with a row for each number.

Phone Numbers → Porting (1): click Continue on a draft (2), or View to open a request (3).

- Action required: your current provider rejected a number, and the request page shows why. The other numbers carry on. To try that number again with corrected details, choose Duplicate in the row's menu. A failed request shows Duplicate to retry instead. A copy keeps your details but not the invoice, the PINs or the account number, so you add those again.

- Cancel request: you can cancel while the request is open, but not shortly before a confirmed port date. A number with a confirmed port date keeps its $10 fee; the numbers without one are refunded to your card.

- Delete draft removes a draft you no longer need.

## After the port

- The numbers land in your name. Change their owner and teams on each number afterwards.

- A ported number starts on Direct line, the System default, like a bought number. See Build a call workflow.

- From then on it is billed like any other number on your workspace. See pricing.

- A ported number is your own number. Deleting it releases it for good.
