URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/get-started-with-sms

# Get started with SMS

CallForges sends and receives SMS from your phone numbers. A contact's replies come back to the same conversation, and every conversation is in the Inbox, under Messaging in the sidebar. Whether a number can send SMS depends on its country and its type.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Which numbers can send SMS

- On Phone Numbers, the Capabilities column shows an SMS chip on every number that can send SMS. A grey or red chip opens the reason and the one thing to do next, such as Add to campaign, Register now or Register business.

- US numbers send SMS once they are registered with the US carriers (A2P 10DLC). See Register for SMS in the US.

- Numbers in many other countries, such as the UK, Australia, Germany and France, send and receive SMS with no registration. The full list is in Send SMS to contacts in other countries.

- Mobile numbers in a country that allows SMS can send it, and so can local numbers in the US and Canada. Toll-free numbers and most landline numbers can't.

- A number you ported in follows the same rules as one you bought.

Phone Numbers: the SMS chip in the Capabilities column (1) marks each number that can send SMS.

## SMS in the free trial

- In the free trial you can send SMS from a number in a country that needs no carrier registration, such as the UK, Australia or Germany. Each SMS is paid from your credits, and you can top up credits at any time.

- Numbers in the US, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands need 10DLC registration first, and you can register during the trial. The carriers' fees are paid by card when you submit. Once its campaign is approved, the number sends SMS in the trial too. See Register for SMS in the US.

- One thing needs a paid plan: the Send SMS step in a call workflow shows Not included in the trial. Upgrade to use it. until you choose a plan.

- If the Inbox reads Messaging is switched off for this workspace. Contact support to turn it on., contact support.

## Where to see your SMS: the Inbox

- Click Inbox, under Messaging in the sidebar. The number beside Inbox counts your unread SMS.

- Pick one of your numbers at the top to see its conversations and whether it can send SMS.

- Open a conversation to read it and reply. Each conversation is one contact and one of your numbers, so a contact who texts two of your numbers has two conversations.

Messaging's settings are in Settings → Messaging settings: Messaging (who gets a conversation, opt-outs, the out-of-hours reply and signatures) and Saved replies.

The Inbox: Inbox under Messaging in the sidebar (1), the number you are on (2) and its conversations (3).

## What SMS costs

- Each SMS you send or receive is charged from your credits, at the rate for the country it reaches.

- A long SMS goes out in parts, and each part is charged as one SMS. See SMS length and sending rules.

- With 0 credits, an SMS is refused until you add credits.

- An SMS the carriers fail to deliver can carry a small fee for the failed message, charged from your credits about two days later.

- Registering US numbers has the carriers' own fees, paid by card, not from your credits. See Registration fees.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/register-for-sms-in-the-us

# Register for SMS in the US (A2P 10DLC)

US carriers block business SMS from a local number that isn't registered. Registering, called A2P 10DLC, means the carriers review your business and a campaign: what you will send, to whom, and how people agreed to get it. Once a campaign is approved, its numbers can send and receive SMS. Your calls work the same whether a number is registered or not.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Before you start

- You need an approved Business profile in the Compliance center, and a role that can Buy and release numbers.

- You can register during the free trial too. The carriers' fees are paid by card when you submit: see Registration fees.

- Only US local numbers are registered. Toll-free numbers can't be, and numbers outside the US don't need it where their country allows SMS.

- A workspace can have up to 5 campaigns, and each number belongs to one campaign.

- Open the Compliance center and find Text messaging (A2P 10DLC), below the Business profile.

- Click Add campaign.

Compliance center: the Text messaging (A2P 10DLC) card (1) and Add campaign (2).

## Fill in the campaign

The campaign's steps are on the left. Click Continue to check a step and go on.

- Campaign details: a campaign name, the use case (such as Customer care, Marketing or Account notifications), two to five sub use cases for a Mixed or Low volume mixed campaign, and the numbers. Only your US numbers that are in no other campaign are listed. Your first campaign also asks How many texts will you send a day? (see business vetting). Before you go on, you accept the content carriers don't allow, such as cannabis, high-risk loans or gambling.

- Sample messages: two to five SMS exactly as your contacts will get them, 20 to 1,024 characters each. Name your business in each one and add "Reply STOP to opt out". Say whether your SMS are about lending money, or contain links or phone numbers.

- User consent: how contacts agree to get your SMS, 40 to 2,048 characters, such as a web form and its address. Opt-in keywords such as START, with the reply contacts get, are optional.

- Description: what you send, to whom and why, 40 to 4,096 characters.

- Review and submit: every step read back with Edit beside it, and the carrier fees. When a fee is due, the button says how much, such as Pay $19.50 and submit. Click it to pay and send the campaign to the carriers.

Campaign details: the steps on the left (1), the use case (2), the numbers (3) and Continue (4).

The form saves itself as a draft while you type and when you leave, so you can stop half-way and come back. Submit for review checks every field and needs at least one number.

## Campaign statuses

- Draft: saved, not sent. Continue it from its row. A draft the carriers sent back shows their reason under its name.

- In review: the carriers are reviewing it, usually for 1 to 3 weeks, and it can't be changed until they answer. Statuses update by themselves. Refresh status checks now, at most once every 10 minutes.

- Approved: its numbers can send SMS. Add more numbers from View unregistered numbers, or from a number's chip on Phone Numbers.

- Rejected: the carriers' reason shows in red under its name. Click Fix and resubmit, correct it and submit again. Each resubmission is charged the $15 review fee again, on your card.

### A number the carriers refused

The carriers sometimes refuse one number of an approved campaign and add the others. The campaign shows it as refused, with their reason, and so does its chip on Phone Numbers. Add it again, to the same campaign or another, from a campaign's numbers or with Add to campaign on its chip. Or click Remove beside it to take it off the campaign.

### Delete a campaign

Delete is in each campaign's menu, whatever its status. It withdraws the campaign from the carriers and stops its monthly fee, and its numbers stop sending SMS.

## Business vetting and the daily limit

Your first campaign asks How many texts will you send a day?

- Under 2,000 a day (the default) registers your business without vetting. Most businesses choose this.

- More than 2,000 a day adds business vetting: an independent firm checks your business for the carriers and gives it a trust score, which sets how many SMS you can send a day.

Without vetting, the carriers let a business send up to about 2,000 SMS a day. The question is asked once, before your business is registered; later campaigns don't ask it.

## When your plan ends

When a plan ends (the free trial expired, you cancelled, or the workspace was suspended for an unpaid invoice), Phone Numbers and Billing show a date in red. On that date your numbers are released and every SMS campaign is deleted, which stops its monthly fee.

To keep both, choose a plan before that date, or pay the open invoice of a suspended workspace. Registering again later means a new campaign review, with its fee, and 1 to 3 weeks of waiting.

## Registration fees

Registering carries the carriers' own fees. They are paid on your card, not from your credits:

Fee | When | Price

Business registration | Once per workspace, with your first campaign | $4.50

Business vetting | Once, only if you chose More than 2,000 a day | $41.50

Campaign review | Each new campaign, and each resubmission of a rejected one. Non-refundable once the carriers take the campaign for review. | $15

Monthly campaign fee | Every month for each approved campaign, until you delete it, on your next invoice | $10 a month ($2.40 for Low volume mixed)

- So your first campaign costs $19.50 to submit, or $61 with business vetting. Each later campaign or resubmission costs $15.

- Review and submit shows each fee and the total due now. Submitting charges your saved card, and the campaign goes to the carriers once the payment goes through. With no card saved, the payment page opens.

- If your card is declined, you see "Payment failed. Update your card." Nothing is submitted, and the campaign goes as soon as a new card pays.

- When a fee is due, only an owner or admin who manages billing can submit. Anyone else is asked to ask one of them.

- Only a fee the carriers never take is refunded to your card. If they reject your business registration, so it is never created, its fee and your campaigns' review fees are refunded. If you delete a campaign before they take it for review, its review fee is refunded. A campaign they reject after taking it for review keeps its review fee. If they don't take a submission, what you paid stays for that campaign's next submit.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/send-and-receive-sms

# Send and receive SMS

Send an SMS to a contact from one of your numbers, and their replies land in the same conversation in the Inbox. You can also schedule an SMS to go out later.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Send an SMS

- Click Inbox, under Messaging in the sidebar.

- Open the contact's conversation, or click New message.

- In New message, pick a contact or type their number, and check From: the number the SMS goes from. It suggests the number that contact last talked to. When more than one of your numbers can send SMS, you can pick another.

- Write your SMS. To insert a text you saved, click Saved replies under the box. Click Expand for a bigger box.

- Click Send, or press Ctrl + Enter (⌘ + Enter on a Mac). Enter starts a new line.

New message: who it's for (1), the From number (2), your SMS (3) and Send (4).

- You send from the numbers you may call from.

- With 0 credits, an SMS is refused until you add credits.

- A contact who replied STOP can't be sent an SMS until they reply START. See SMS opt-outs.

## Receive SMS and replies from contacts

When a contact replies, or sends an SMS to one of your numbers that can receive it, it lands in the Inbox, in that contact's conversation for that number, and shows as unread. A closed or archived conversation reopens when the contact sends an SMS again. Received SMS are charged like the ones you send.

## Delivery status

Under each SMS you send, the conversation shows where it is:

- Sending: on its way.

- Sent: the carrier took it, and its delivery isn't reported yet.

- Delivered: it reached the contact's phone.

- Not delivered: it didn't arrive, and the reason shows under it, such as a phone that is off, a landline or a number that no longer exists. Click Try again to send it once more from the same number. Each SMS can be sent again once.

- Not confirmed yet: the carrier didn't answer when the SMS was sent, so we are checking whether it went out. It is never sent twice. Within about 10 minutes it shows what happened, or turns to Not delivered with We couldn't confirm this text was sent. Check with the contact before you try again.

- Scheduled: it goes out at the time shown under it.

A conversation: each SMS shows its status under it (1), and Try again on one that wasn't delivered (2).

## Long SMS

The counter under the message box shows how many SMS your message goes out as and the characters used, for example 2 texts · 161 / 306. A long message goes out in parts that the contact's phone joins into one, each part charged as one SMS, up to 10 parts. Your signature counts toward it. See SMS length and sending rules.

## Schedule an SMS

- Write your SMS, click the arrow beside Send and choose Schedule….

- Pick the Date and Time: at least 2 minutes from now and at most a year ahead.

- Click Schedule.

Schedule text: pick the Date (1) and Time (2), then click Schedule (3).

- The SMS shows in the conversation marked Scheduled, and the Scheduled tab lists the conversations that have one.

- Until it goes out, the user who scheduled it, or a user who can manage texting settings, can edit its text and time or cancel it.

- At its time it goes from the same number, with the signature of the user who scheduled it. It is checked again then: if the contact replied STOP, the number can no longer send SMS, or your credits ran out, it isn't sent and shows Not delivered with the reason. Credits are charged only for an SMS that goes out.

## Drafts

What you write in a conversation and don't send is kept as your draft, on any device, and the conversation shows Draft: in the list. The Drafts tab lists the conversations where you have one. Your drafts are yours alone. Sending the SMS, scheduling it or clearing the box deletes the draft.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/the-messaging-inbox

# The Messaging Inbox

The Inbox holds the SMS conversations of the numbers you can use. Each conversation is one contact and one of your numbers, with every SMS between them, sent and received.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Tabs and labels

Pick a number at the top, then a tab:

- Open: every conversation that isn't closed or archived.

- Assigned to me and Unassigned.

- Drafts: the conversations where you started an SMS and didn't send it.

- Scheduled: the conversations with an SMS waiting to go out.

- Closed and Archived, under More when the window is narrow.

In the list, a blue dot and a blue time mean unread SMS. Opted out means the contact replied STOP. Delivery failed, in red, means your last SMS didn't arrive: open the conversation to see why and click Try again.

The Inbox: the tabs (1), the filters (2) and a conversation's labels (3).

## Search and filters

- Search by name or number.

- Number, Assigned to and Unread.

- Replies: With replies shows the conversations where the contact has sent you an SMS at least once; Without replies, those where they never have.

- The date of the last SMS.

Every filter works with every tab. Click Clear filters to start again.

## Assign a conversation

In a conversation, click Assign and pick a user, or pick Unassigned. Who gets a new conversation by itself is a setting: see Who gets a new SMS conversation.

## Close, reopen or archive an SMS conversation

- Close a conversation when it's done. It moves to Closed, and you can reopen it.

- Archive one to put it away, such as spam or a contact you won't write to again. It leaves Open and Closed for Archived. Unarchive brings it back. An archived conversation can't be closed or reopened until you unarchive it.

- Both come back by themselves: when the contact sends an SMS again, a closed or archived conversation reopens in Open.

- Mark as unread to come back to it later.

## Bulk actions on many conversations

- Tick the conversations you want, up to 100 at a time.

- Choose Close, Reopen, Archive, Unarchive, Mark read or Mark unread.

Each conversation changes as if you had done it on its own, so one that can't change doesn't stop the others, and you are told which didn't change and why. Bulk actions don't send SMS: each SMS goes to one contact.

Tick conversations (1), then choose an action (2).

## Who sees which numbers

You see the SMS of the numbers you may call from, and you send from them. A user whose role has Read the texts of every number in the workspace sees every number's SMS, a colleague's numbers included. Sending, assigning and closing need Send texts and assign, close, reopen and mark conversations. Roles are set in Settings → Roles & permissions.

## Calls aren't in the Inbox

The Inbox holds SMS only. A missed call shows in the bell of each user it rang, and every call is in Call History.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/who-gets-a-new-sms-conversation

# Who gets a new SMS conversation

Who an SMS conversation is assigned to is set in Settings → Messaging settings → Messaging, under Conversations. The setting is the same for every number in the workspace.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## New conversations

When a contact sends you the first SMS, the conversation is assigned by the rule under New conversations. Pick one:

- Remain assigned (the default): the conversation waits unassigned until a user replies, then stays with whoever replied last. When another user replies, it moves to them.

- First response: the conversation waits unassigned until a user replies, and the first user who replies keeps it.

- Round robin: the conversation goes at once to the number's users, in turn. Replies don't move it.

Click Save changes.

Settings → Messaging: New conversations (1) and the three switches below it (2).

## When you start a conversation

With Assign a conversation to whoever starts it on (the default), a conversation you start from New message is yours. Turn it off to leave such conversations unassigned.

## When a conversation closes or the contact opts out

- Unassign when a conversation is closed or archived (on by default): closing or archiving a conversation clears its assignee. When the contact sends an SMS again, it reopens unassigned.

- Unassign when the contact opts out (on by default): when a contact replies STOP, their conversations on every number are unassigned.

## Who can change these settings

Anyone who can read SMS sees these settings. Changing them needs Manage texting settings and saved replies in the user's role. To assign one conversation by hand, see Assign a conversation.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/sms-opt-outs-stop-and-start

# SMS opt-outs: STOP and START

A contact who replies STOP stops getting your SMS, from every number in your workspace, until they reply START.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## When a contact replies STOP

- A reply of STOP, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END, QUIT or a similar word opts the contact out.

- From then on, an SMS to them is refused before it goes, from any of your numbers, and no automatic reply is sent to them. Their conversation shows Opted out.

- On a number outside the US and Canada, a reply counts only when the whole SMS is one such word: "Stop." counts, "please stop texting me" doesn't. No confirmation SMS goes back to the contact.

## Opt back in: when a contact replies START

A reply of START, YES or UNSTOP lifts the opt-out, and you can send them SMS again.

## When a contact replies HELP

A contact who replies HELP isn't opted out. Their SMS lands in the Inbox like any other, so answer it there.

## Unassign or archive on opt-out

Both are in Settings → Messaging settings → Messaging:

- Unassign when the contact opts out, under Conversations (on by default): the contact's conversations are unassigned on every number.

- Archive the conversation when the contact opts out, set for each number under Out-of-hours reply: the contact's conversation on that number moves to Archived.

## The list of opted-out contacts

- Open Settings → Messaging settings → Messaging.

- Under Opt-outs, the count of opted-out contacts shows. Click View list.

Opted-out contacts lists each contact's number and when they opted out. A contact the carriers blocked shows Blocked by the carrier.

Opted-out contacts: each contact's number and when they opted out (1).

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/sms-out-of-hours-reply

# Out-of-hours SMS reply

Each number can send an automatic SMS reply to contacts who write to it while it is closed, such as "Thanks for your message. We're closed right now and will reply after 9 AM."

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Set up the reply

- Open Settings → Messaging settings → Messaging.

- Under Out-of-hours reply, pick the number.

- Turn on Out-of-hours reply.

- Set the number's Opening hours: the open days, their times and the Time zone.

- Write the reply in Out-of-hours reply text, up to 320 characters.

- Click Save changes.

Out-of-hours reply: the number (1), the switch (2), the reply's text (3) and its opening hours (4).

## How often it is sent

- A contact who writes while the number is closed gets the reply at most once every 24 hours from that number, however many SMS they send.

- Contacts who replied STOP never get it, and an SMS that says only STOP, START or HELP gets no reply.

- If the reply can't go out when their SMS arrives, it is tried again until it goes. 24 hours after their SMS it is marked Not sent instead.

## Its signature and length

The number's own signature is added to the reply, and the two together must fit in one message of up to 10 parts. See SMS signatures and saved replies.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/sms-signatures-and-saved-replies

# SMS signatures and saved replies

A signature is added to the end of the SMS your users send. Saved replies are SMS you write once and insert in any conversation.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Add a signature

- Open Settings → Messaging settings → Messaging and find Signatures.

- Click Add signature.

- Give it a Name and its Text, up to 160 characters.

- Choose where it applies: a User, a Number or both. One user on one number; one user on every number, so each user can have their own; or one number, for everyone who sends from it.

One signature is on at a time for each of these: turning one on turns the earlier one off.

Add signature: Name (1), Text (2), and the User and Number it applies to (3).

## Which signature is used

Only one signature is added to an SMS. A signature for the user on that number wins, then the user's own, then the number's. The out-of-hours reply carries the number's signature.

## Signatures count toward the length

The signature goes on a new line at the end of the SMS, so it counts toward its characters and the number of parts it goes out as, up to 10. See SMS length and sending rules.

## Saved replies

- Open Settings → Messaging settings → Saved replies and click Add saved reply.

- Give it a Name and its Text, and save it.

- In any conversation, click Saved replies under the message box and pick one to insert it. Search by its name or its words.

Settings → Saved replies: your saved replies (1) and Add saved reply (2).

## Who can change them

- A user whose role has Manage texting settings and saved replies manages every signature and every saved reply.

- Other users add, edit and delete only their own signatures, on the numbers they can send from, and insert any saved reply.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/sms-to-other-countries

# Send SMS to contacts in other countries

You can often send SMS to contacts in other countries, but your number doesn't always show. The carriers in the contact's country decide what they see and whether they can reply, by that country's rules.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Which countries' numbers can send SMS

A number sends SMS when the carriers let it (mobile numbers, and local numbers in the US and Canada) and its country is one of these:

- Sending and receiving, with no registration: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Jersey, Lithuania, Mexico, Myanmar, the Netherlands, Norway, the Philippines, Poland, Portugal, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand and the UK. Canadian local and mobile numbers send SMS with no registration, in the free trial too.

- The US, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands: once the number is registered (A2P 10DLC). See Register for SMS in the US.

- India, Malaysia and Singapore: not yet. Their carriers need a registration CallForges doesn't offer yet.

- Every other country, such as Ireland, Japan or Iceland: their numbers can't send SMS.

Toll-free numbers and most landline numbers can't send SMS. On Phone Numbers, each number that can has the SMS chip, and the Inbox says why a number can't.

## What a contact in India, France or the UK sees

- Your number, and they can reply: Germany, Spain, the Netherlands, Ireland, Portugal, Switzerland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Australia and Japan, among others.

- Another number or a generic sender instead of yours, so their reply never reaches you: India (a random short number), France, Belgium, Finland, Poland, New Zealand, Mexico, Brazil, Singapore, South Africa and Israel, among others.

- SMS from a foreign number aren't accepted, so the SMS shows Not delivered: the UK, Italy, Austria, the Philippines, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, among others.

The carriers change these rules from time to time.

## Contacts in the US

A number outside the US can't send SMS to the US, Puerto Rico or the US Virgin Islands. The SMS is refused before it goes: US carriers don't accept texts from numbers outside the US. Text from a US number.

## Send from a number in the contact's country

- An SMS to a contact in your number's own country usually carries your number. Mexico is the exception: its carriers replace it too.

- To reach a contact abroad as yourself and get their replies, send from a number in their country, where that country's numbers can send SMS.

- New message suggests the number that contact last talked to, not one from their country, so check From before you send.

## What it costs

An SMS is charged from your credits at the rate for the country it reaches, whichever number sends it.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/sms-length-and-sending-rules

# SMS length and sending rules

What fits in one SMS, how a longer message is sent, and the checks every SMS passes before it goes.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 14 November 2026

## Characters per SMS

- One SMS holds 160 characters.

- With an emoji, or letters outside the standard SMS alphabet (such as Chinese, Arabic, Hindi or some accented letters), it holds 70.

## Long messages in parts

- A longer message goes out in parts that the contact's phone joins into one: 153 characters a part, or 67 with an emoji or another alphabet.

- Each part is charged as one SMS.

- A message can be up to 1,600 characters and 10 parts, your signature included. A longer one reads Too long: a text can be up to 10 parts.

## The counter under the message box

As you write, the counter under the message box shows how many SMS the message goes out as and the characters used, for example 2 texts · 161 / 306: two SMS, 161 characters of the 306 that two parts hold.

The counter under the message box (1): how many SMS, then the characters used.

## Quiet hours: SMS at night

An SMS goes out when you send it, or at the time you scheduled it, whatever the hour where the contact is. Some countries limit marketing SMS to certain hours or days, such as Italy, Brazil and South Africa, so check the rules of your contacts' country and schedule SMS for their daytime.

## What is checked before an SMS goes

- The number can send SMS, and you may send from it.

- The contact hasn't replied STOP. See SMS opt-outs.

- You have credits. With 0 credits, an SMS is refused until you add credits.

- A contact in the US is sent SMS only from a US number.

A scheduled SMS is checked again at its time. An SMS refused by one of these checks never leaves, so it costs nothing. An SMS the carriers fail to deliver after it leaves can carry a small fee for the failed message, charged from your credits about two days later.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/invite-users

# Invite users

Invite your teammates by e-mail to work in your CallForges workspace. Each person gets a link to join, with the role you chose for them.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- Users with the Owner or Admin role can invite users. A custom role can too, if it has the permission to invite.

- In the free trial, until you choose a plan, the invite dialog reads Upgrade to invite teammates. An owner or admin who manages billing can click Choose a plan there.

- On a paid plan, each new user is a seat on your plan. See Plans and seats.

- Invite people with their work e-mail address. A personal address may be refused with Invite people with their work email.

## Send an invite

- Open Settings, then Users & teams, and stay on the Users tab.

- Click Invite user.

- In Email addresses, type an address and press Enter, a comma or a space. Add as many as you need.

- Pick a Role. Everyone in this invite gets the same role.

- Click Send invite, or Send N invites for several people.

Invite to workspace: type the Email addresses (step 3), pick a Role (step 4), then click Send invite (step 5).

You see Invite sent, and each person appears in the list with the status Invite pending. If someone is already in the workspace, CallForges tells you and doesn't invite them again.

## Choose a role

Role | What they can do

Owner | Everything, including creating custom roles. There is one owner per workspace, so you can't invite someone as owner.

Admin | Runs the workspace day to day: buys and assigns numbers, invites and removes users, edits teams and workspace settings, and sees everyone's calls, campaigns and contacts.

Member | Does the calling: creates and runs campaigns, works with contacts and lists, logs call outcomes and notes, and listens to recordings. Can't buy numbers, invite people or change workspace settings.

Custom roles | Roles your owner made in Settings → Roles & permissions, with exactly the permissions they need.

You can only give a role up to your own. An admin can invite admins and members. A custom role can only give the permissions it holds itself.

## When a seat is needed

On a paid plan, the invite dialog reminds you that each new user is a seat on your plan, and that if no paid seat is free, you pay for one before the invite is sent.

- If a paid seat is free, for example after someone was removed, the new user takes it at no extra charge.

- If no seat is free, CallForges opens a checkout for the seats you need and shows the amount before you pay. Once the payment goes through, you see Your invite is on its way.

- If you can't manage billing, you see A seat is needed. Ask an owner or admin who manages billing to add one.

- If you see Your workspace has reached its user limit — contact support, write to our support team.

## What the invited user does

- They open the link in the invite e-mail. The page reads Join and your workspace name.

- New to CallForges: they enter their First name, Last name, Username and Password, and click Create account and join.

- Already have an account with that address: they click Sign in. If they are signed in with a different account, they click Sign out and continue first.

If the page reads This invitation is no longer valid, the invite expired or was revoked. Send them a new one.

## Resend or revoke an invite

- Click Invited above the list to see only pending invites.

- Open a row's menu and click Resend invite to send the e-mail again.

- Click Revoke invite, then Revoke, to cancel it. Their invite link stops working immediately.

Click Invited (1) to see pending invites. A row's menu has Resend invite (2) and Revoke invite (3).

To remove someone who already joined, open their row's menu and choose Remove from workspace. They lose access immediately. Their call history and campaigns stay, and their numbers move to the workspace owner. To add a user to a team, use the Teams tab.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/plans-and-seats

# Plans and seats

Your workspace has one plan, and every user in it is a seat on that plan. You pay per seat, monthly or annually, by card. This article shows how to choose a plan, add seats and change your plan later.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- By default, only users with the Owner or Admin role see Billing in the sidebar and can change the plan, the seats or the card.

- Only the Owner can cancel the subscription.

- To compare everything each plan includes, see Pricing.

## The plans

Plan | Billed monthly | Billed annually | Free minutes

Starter | $19 | $15 | 100

Business | $39 | $29 | 500

Scale | $59 | $45 | 1,000

Prices are per user per month. Free minutes are per user each month, for inbound and outbound calls to and from the US, the UK, Canada and Australia. Your workspace's free minutes are one pool: the plan's minutes times your paid seats. They reset each billing month and don't roll over. Calls beyond them, and calls to other countries, are paid from credits.

Billing → Pricing shows the prices for your workspace. Switch between Monthly and Annually to compare; annual billing saves up to 25%.

Each paid seat also includes one free local number in the US, the UK, Canada or Australia. Other numbers have a monthly price: you pay the full monthly price when you buy one, your next invoice skips it, and after that it's charged to your card with your plan.

## How seats work

- A seat is every user in the workspace, including people you invited who haven't joined yet.

- Every seat is on the workspace's plan. You can't put different users on different plans.

- There's no seat minimum. The Owner is always one seat.

- When you remove a user, their seat stays paid until the end of the billing period. The next user you add takes it at no extra charge.

- At each renewal, you pay for the users you have then.

In Billing → Overview, Plan details shows your seats, how many are paid and unused, and your workspace's user limit (Capacity up to). To raise the limit, click Contact support to raise it.

Plan details: your seats and how many are paid and unused (1), your user limit (2), and Contact support to raise it (3).

## Choose a plan

- Open Billing → Pricing and click Choose Starter, Choose Business or Choose Scale. You can also click Subscribe now in Plan details.

- Plan and seats: pick Monthly or Annually and the plan. The list shows every seat you'll pay for, with a subtotal. Click Continue.

- Billing details: enter the billing name, email, address and country for your invoices. Click Continue.

- Payment: check the Amount due today and the amount that recurs, then click Confirm and pay and pay by card.

Plan and seats: pick Monthly or Annually and the plan, then click Continue (step 2).

Your plan starts at once, and so does your billing cycle. Renewals are charged to the same card automatically. To change the card, click Update card under Payment method. In the free trial you can instead add a card and start the plan when the trial ends: see Start your free trial.

## Add seats

You need a free paid seat for each new user. There are two ways to get one:

- In Billing → Overview, click Add seats, set the Number of seats and click Confirm and pay. Then invite users from Settings → Users & teams.

- Click Invite user and send the invite. If no paid seat is free, CallForges opens the seat payment for you, and the invite goes out once it's paid. See Invite users.

Billing → Overview: click Add seats (1), or Invite user (2) to send an invite and pay for a seat if none is free.

Today you pay only for the rest of the current billing period. The payment step shows the Amount due today and the dates it covers. After that, the seat renews with your plan.

## Upgrade or downgrade

- Upgrade: on Billing → Pricing, click Upgrade on a higher plan, then Continue to payment. You pay the difference for your paid seats for the rest of the billing period. Every seat moves at once, and the extra minutes are added to this period's pool.

- Downgrade: click Downgrade on a lower plan, then Downgrade at renewal. Your workspace keeps its plan until the renewal date, then every seat moves. Until then, Plan details shows the change with an Undo button.

- Monthly to annual: click Switch to annual in Plan details, or switch Pricing to Annually and pick a plan. The annual plan starts today, and your unused monthly time is credited against the year.

- Annual to monthly: click Switch to monthly at renewal. It changes at your annual renewal, and Stay annual undoes it.

Billing → Pricing: Upgrade (1) or Downgrade (2) on another plan. Annually (3) shows the annual prices.

## If a payment fails, or you cancel

- Seats, an upgrade and a switch to annual are charged to your saved card at once, never from credits. With no card saved, the payment page opens. If the card is declined, you see "Payment failed. Update your card." and nothing is changed: update your card under Payment method, then try again.

- Only a user who manages billing can pay. Anyone else is asked to ask an owner or admin.

- If a renewal can't be charged, a banner says "Payment failed. Pay by" with a date. Click Pay now, or update your card under Payment method. A new card is tried at once.

- If that date passes, the workspace is suspended: calls and campaigns stop until the amount due is paid. Owners and admins can still sign in and pay from Billing → Overview, and the workspace comes back on its own once the payment goes through.

- To cancel, the Owner clicks Cancel subscription on Billing → Overview and confirms. Everything keeps working until the end of the billing period. After that, calls and campaigns stop until you choose a plan again. Until then, Revoke cancellation keeps your plan. Payments are non-refundable.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/add-credits

# Add credits

Credits are your workspace's prepaid balance for usage, such as calls beyond your free minutes. Your plan and seats are charged to your card separately. Top up whenever you like, and see every charge in Billing.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 31 October 2026

## Before you start

- By default, only users with the Owner or Admin role can see and add credits.

- You can add credits at any time, including during the free trial.

## What credits pay for

One credit is worth $1.

- Calls beyond your plan's free minutes.

- Calls to and from countries other than the US, the UK, Canada and Australia. These never use free minutes.

- Call transcripts and AI call summaries. During the free trial, transcripts of calls on your trial minutes are free; AI call summaries are not.

- SMS, sent and received.

Your plan, your seats, your phone numbers' monthly price and one-time fees such as porting a number don't come out of credits. They are charged to your card: see Plans and seats.

## Add credits

- Open Add credits from any of these places: click Credits in the sidebar and choose Add credits; click Add credits on Available credits in Billing → Overview; or click Add credits on the banner when your credits reach 0.

- Pick one of the amounts, or type a whole number of credits in Other amount. The line under it shows the smallest and largest amount you can add.

- Check You pay, your Current balance and your New balance.

- Click Continue to payment and pay by card. The cards and wallets you can use are shown above the button.

- Wait while it says Confirming your payment…. When it says the credits were added, click Done.

Add credits: pick an amount or type one in Other amount (step 2), check You pay and your New balance (step 3), then click Continue to payment (step 4).

Payments are charged in US dollars (USD): $1 buys 1 credit. Credits are added as soon as the payment is confirmed. If you close the window while it's confirming, the credits are still added. The receipt is on Billing → Invoices.

If you see Payment didn't go through, nothing was added. Click Try again, or use another card.

## See your balance and usage

- The Credits pill in the sidebar shows your balance. It turns red at 0.

- Billing → Overview shows your Available credits.

- Billing → Usage balance has Paid credit use: every top-up and every charge beyond your free minutes. Filter it by item and date (it opens on the last 7 days), and click Export to download it.

A call charge marked Estimated may be corrected later, up or down, once the call's final price is known.

If a top-up is refunded to your card, its credits leave your balance at the same moment, on a row named Refunded top-up. Only credits you haven't spent can be refunded.

Billing → Usage balance → Paid credit use: click Export (1) to download it. A charge marked Estimated (2) may be corrected later.

## When credits run out

A red banner says "Your credits are at 0 — recharge to keep calling." Then:

- Calls your free minutes cover keep working.

- An outbound call that needs credits isn't placed, and you see You're out of credits.

- A running campaign stops. Leads not called yet stay in the queue, so you can resume it after you add credits.

- Incoming calls still ring, so your balance can go below 0.

- New calls aren't transcribed, except calls on your trial minutes. The call shows "Not transcribed — your credits were at 0." After you add credits, open the call and click Generate transcript.

When your credits reach 0, a red banner appears at the top of every page. Click Add credits (1) on it to top up.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/attio-integration

# Attio integration

The Attio integration logs every call you make or take in CallForges onto the matching person in Attio, as a note or as a record of a Calls object. It also lets you browse your Attio people inside CallForges and import them as contacts to call.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 22 November 2026

## Before you start

- You need a CallForges owner or admin role to connect, configure or disconnect Attio. Other users don't see the integration settings, but their calls are logged once they are mapped.

- You need access to the Attio workspace you want to connect, with permission to install apps.

- One CallForges workspace connects to one Attio workspace.

## Connect Attio

Connect from CallForges with the steps below, or find CallForges in Attio's app marketplace: CallForges on Attio.

- In CallForges, open Integrations and choose Attio.

- Click Connect. Attio opens in the same tab.

- Sign in to Attio if asked, pick the Attio workspace, and click Allow.

- You come back to the Connection tab, which shows the Attio workspace, who connected it and when.

If the Attio workspace is already connected to another CallForges workspace, CallForges asks before moving it. That other workspace then stops logging calls to Attio.

If Attio later asks CallForges to sign in again (for example, after the app was removed in Attio), the Connection tab shows Reconnect. Calls made in the meantime wait and are sent once you reconnect.

Attio before it is connected: click Connect.

The Connection tab after connecting Attio.

## Map users

Calls are logged only for CallForges users who are matched to an Attio workspace member. Open the Map users tab:

- Click Auto-map by e-mail to match every user whose e-mail address is the same in both products.

- For anyone left, choose their Attio member from the list, or leave them on Not mapped.

- Click Save.

Calls by an unmapped user are skipped, and each skip shows up in Activity with the reason. Use Show unmapped only to find the users who still need a match. After you map them, you can send their skipped calls from Activity.

Map users: match each CallForges user to their Attio member.

## Call logging settings

Open the Settings tab, change what you need and click Save changes.

### Workflow: what each call becomes

Choose separately for outbound answered calls, outbound unanswered calls, inbound answered calls, missed calls and voicemails:

Option | What is written in Attio

Note | A note on the person's record with the direction, outcome, talk time, the user who made or took the call, the disposition and the call notes.

Custom object | A record in a Calls object, linked to the person, with Summary, AI summary, Direction, Outcome, Disposition, Notes, Duration, From, To, Agent, Recording and Transcript attributes. CallForges creates the Calls object in your Attio workspace the first time you save this option. Nothing is created in Attio until then.

Don't log | Nothing. The call is not written to Attio.

Name your Calls records (once). Attio's API can't choose which attribute names a record, so new Calls records show their record ID until you set it. In Attio, open Settings → Data → Objects → Calls → Appearance and set Record text to Summary. Existing records are renamed too.

### What each note includes

- Link to the recording adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the recording plays.

- Link to the transcript adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the transcript is read.

- AI summary adds the call's AI summary, when it has one. Summaries are made for English calls long enough to summarise, on plans that include them.

Recordings and transcripts stay in CallForges. They are not copied into Attio, and only signed-in users of your CallForges workspace can open the links.

### Connected numbers

Leave Log calls on all numbers on to log calls on every number your workspace owns, including numbers bought later. Turn it off to pick the numbers to log. Calls on numbers that aren't picked are skipped.

### When calls are logged

A call is written to Attio within a few minutes of ending, so the disposition and notes the user adds after the call are included. If the call is changed later, for example a new disposition, the note or Calls record is updated to match.

Settings → Workflow: choose what each kind of call becomes in Attio.

## The caller's name when a call rings

When someone who isn't in your CallForges Contacts calls one of your numbers, CallForges looks the number up in Attio while the call rings, and the name appears on the ring card a moment later.

The ring never waits for the answer. If Attio is slow or busy, or several people share the number, the card shows the number alone. A contact saved in CallForges always comes first. CallForges keeps the answer in memory for a few minutes and doesn't save it.

## Unknown numbers

CallForges finds the Attio person by phone number. In Settings → General:

- Create an Attio person if the number isn't found: when no person in Attio has the number, CallForges creates one so the call is still logged. When this is off, the call isn't logged and Activity shows that the person wasn't found.

- Use the phone number as the new person's name: used when CallForges has no name for the caller. When this is off, the new person is named "Unknown caller". This applies only while creating people is on.

- Add Attio people to CallForges Contacts: when a call reaches someone who is in Attio but not in your CallForges Contacts, CallForges adds them to Contacts and links the two. Off by default.

Settings → General: unknown numbers, Contacts and what each entry includes.

## Import contacts

The Contacts tab lists the people in your Attio workspace who have a phone number, read live from Attio. Each row shows whether the person is already in CallForges, with a link to open them in Attio.

- Search, or filter by an Attio list with All lists.

- Select people, or import everyone in the chosen list.

- Click Import and choose an existing CallForges list or name a new one.

Imported people become CallForges contacts linked to their Attio records, ready to call from a campaign or the dialer. Click Sync now to bring in later changes. CallForges doesn't copy your Attio data on a schedule; it reads Attio only when you open the tab, import or sync.

The Contacts tab: your Attio people with a phone number, ready to import.

## Log past calls

Connecting logs the calls that happen from then on. To send calls your workspace made before you connected, use Settings → Log past calls:

- Under How far back, pick a date range. It reaches back up to 1 year.

- Click Log past calls. CallForges counts the calls first and shows how many would be logged, and which users' calls would be skipped because they aren't mapped.

- Confirm. A progress bar shows the calls being sent.

Past calls are sent in the background and never delay the logging of new calls. To stop a run, open Activity, go to the Queued tab and click Stop queued.

Log past calls: pick how far back, then confirm.

## Activity

The Activity tab lists every call and what happened to it in Attio: logged (and whether as a note or a Calls record), queued, failed or skipped, with the reason. You can retry one call, or use Retry all for every failed or skipped call that matches your filters. Never logged lists calls that were never sent to Attio.

Activity: what happened to each call in Attio.

## Disconnect

- Open Integrations → Attio.

- Click Disconnect and confirm.

Calls stop being logged to Attio and the user mapping is cleared. CallForges gives up its access to your Attio workspace. Notes and Calls records already written stay in Attio, and your logging settings are kept in case you reconnect. You can also remove the CallForges app from your Attio workspace settings at any time; CallForges then shows Reconnect.

The Disconnect confirmation.

## What CallForges can access

When you click Allow, CallForges asks Attio for these permissions on your workspace:

Permission | Why

`record_permission:read-write` | Find the person by phone number, create a person for an unknown number when you turn that on, and write Calls records.

`object_configuration:read-write` | Read your objects and attributes, and create the Calls object when you choose Custom object.

`note:read-write` | Write the call note, and replace it when the call changes.

`user_management:read` | List workspace members for Map users and Auto-map by e-mail.

`list_configuration:read` | Show your Attio lists in the Contacts tab's list filter.

`list_entry:read` | Read who is in a list, to filter and import by list.

Your Attio access is stored encrypted and used only for the features above. See our Privacy Policy.

---

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/hubspot-integration

# HubSpot integration

The HubSpot integration logs every call you make or take in CallForges on the timeline of the matching HubSpot contact, as a HubSpot call or as a note. It also lets you browse your HubSpot contacts inside CallForges and import them as contacts to call.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 22 October 2026

## Before you start

- You need a CallForges owner or admin role to connect, configure or disconnect HubSpot. Other users don't see the integration settings, but their calls are logged once they are mapped.

- You need a HubSpot user who is allowed to install apps in the HubSpot account, such as a Super Admin.

- One CallForges workspace connects to one HubSpot account.

## Connect HubSpot

- In CallForges, open Integrations and choose HubSpot.

- Click Connect. HubSpot opens in the same tab.

- Sign in to HubSpot if asked, choose the HubSpot account, review the permissions and click Connect app. While the app is waiting for HubSpot Marketplace review, HubSpot may ask you to confirm that you want to install it.

- You come back to the Connection tab, which shows the HubSpot account, who connected it and when.

If the HubSpot account is already connected to another CallForges workspace, CallForges asks before moving it. That other workspace then stops logging calls to HubSpot.

If HubSpot later asks CallForges to sign in again (for example, after the app was uninstalled in HubSpot), the Connection tab shows Reconnect. Calls made in the meantime wait and are sent once you reconnect.

HubSpot before it is connected: click Connect.

The Connection tab after connecting HubSpot.

## Map users

Calls are logged only for CallForges users who are matched to a HubSpot owner. The owner becomes the owner of the logged call in HubSpot. Open the Map users tab:

- Click Auto-map by e-mail to match every user whose e-mail address is the same in both products.

- For anyone left, choose their HubSpot owner from the list, or leave them on Not mapped.

- Click Save.

Calls by an unmapped user are skipped, and each skip shows up in Activity with the reason. Use Show unmapped only to find the users who still need a match. After you map them, you can send their skipped calls from Activity.

Map users: match each CallForges user to their HubSpot owner.

## Call logging settings

Open the Settings tab, change what you need and click Save changes.

### Workflow: what each call becomes

Choose separately for outbound answered calls, outbound unanswered calls, inbound answered calls, missed calls and voicemails:

Option | What is written in HubSpot

Call activity | A HubSpot call on the contact's timeline, with its direction, outcome, duration, owner, the disposition and the call notes. It counts in HubSpot's own call reports.

Note | A note on the contact's timeline with the same details written as text.

Don't log | Nothing. The call is not written to HubSpot.

### What each logged call includes

- Link to the recording adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the recording plays.

- Link to the transcript adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the transcript is read.

- AI summary adds the call's AI summary, when it has one. Summaries are made for English calls long enough to summarise, on plans that include them.

Recordings and transcripts stay in CallForges. They are not copied into HubSpot, and only signed-in users of your CallForges workspace can open the links.

### Connected numbers

Leave Log calls on all numbers on to log calls on every number your workspace owns, including numbers bought later. Turn it off to pick the numbers to log. Calls on numbers that aren't picked are skipped.

### When calls are logged

A call is written to HubSpot within a few minutes of ending, so the disposition and notes the user adds after the call are included. If the call is changed later, for example a new disposition, the same HubSpot call or note is updated.

Settings → Workflow: choose what each kind of call becomes in HubSpot.

## The caller's name when a call rings

When someone who isn't in your CallForges Contacts calls one of your numbers, CallForges looks the number up in HubSpot while the call rings, and the name appears on the ring card a moment later.

The ring never waits for the answer. If HubSpot is slow or busy, or several contacts share the number, the card shows the number alone. A contact saved in CallForges always comes first. CallForges keeps the answer in memory for a few minutes and doesn't save it.

## Unknown numbers

CallForges finds the HubSpot contact by its phone or mobile number. In Settings → General:

- Create a HubSpot contact if the number isn't found: when no contact in HubSpot has the number, CallForges creates one so the call is still logged. When this is off, the call isn't logged and Activity shows that the contact wasn't found.

- Use the phone number as the new contact's name: used when CallForges has no name for the caller. When this is off, the new contact is named "Unknown caller". This applies only while creating contacts is on.

- Add HubSpot contacts to CallForges Contacts: when a call reaches someone who is in HubSpot but not in your CallForges Contacts, CallForges adds them to Contacts and links the two. Off by default.

New contacts count toward your HubSpot account's contact limits like any other contact.

Settings → General: unknown numbers, Contacts and what each entry includes.

## Import contacts

The Contacts tab lists the contacts in your HubSpot account who have a phone number, read live from HubSpot. Each row shows the contact's company and whether they are already in CallForges, with a link to open them in HubSpot.

- Search, or filter by a HubSpot list with All lists.

- Select contacts, or import everyone in the chosen list.

- Click Import and choose an existing CallForges list or name a new one.

Imported contacts become CallForges contacts linked to their HubSpot records, ready to call from a campaign or the dialer. Click Sync now to bring in later changes. CallForges doesn't copy your HubSpot data on a schedule; it reads HubSpot only when you open the tab, import or sync.

The list filter needs the optional lists permission. If you didn't grant it when connecting, the filter says so; reconnect HubSpot to grant it.

The Contacts tab: your HubSpot contacts with a phone number, ready to import.

## Log past calls

Connecting logs the calls that happen from then on. To send calls your workspace made before you connected, use Settings → Log past calls:

- Under How far back, pick a date range. It reaches back up to 1 year.

- Click Log past calls. CallForges counts the calls first and shows how many would be logged, and which users' calls would be skipped because they aren't mapped.

- Confirm. A progress bar shows the calls being sent.

Past calls are sent in the background and never delay the logging of new calls. To stop a run, open Activity, go to the Queued tab and click Stop queued.

Log past calls: pick how far back, then confirm.

## Activity

The Activity tab lists every call and what happened to it in HubSpot: logged (and whether as a call or a note), queued, failed or skipped, with the reason. You can retry one call, or use Retry all for every failed or skipped call that matches your filters. Never logged lists calls that were never sent to HubSpot.

If your HubSpot account's daily API limit is used up, CallForges pauses and shows how many calls are waiting. They are sent automatically once HubSpot accepts requests again. Nothing is lost.

Activity: what happened to each call in HubSpot.

## Disconnect

- Open Integrations → HubSpot.

- Click Disconnect and confirm.

Calls stop being logged to HubSpot and the user mapping is cleared. CallForges gives up its access to your HubSpot account. Calls and notes already written stay in HubSpot, and your logging settings are kept in case you reconnect. You can also uninstall the app from HubSpot (Settings → Integrations → Connected apps) at any time; CallForges then shows Reconnect.

The Disconnect confirmation.

## What CallForges can access

When you connect, CallForges asks HubSpot for these permissions on your account:

Permission | Why

`oauth` | Connect the app to your account.

`crm.objects.contacts.read` | Find the contact by phone number and list contacts in the Contacts tab.

`crm.objects.contacts.write` | Log calls and notes on contacts, and create a contact for an unknown number when you turn that on.

`crm.objects.companies.read` | Show each contact's company in the Contacts tab and on imported contacts.

`crm.objects.owners.read` | List HubSpot owners for Map users and Auto-map by e-mail, and set the owner of each logged call.

`crm.lists.read` (optional) | Show your HubSpot lists in the Contacts tab's list filter.

Your HubSpot access is stored encrypted and used only for the features above. See our Privacy Policy.

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/pipedrive-integration

# Pipedrive integration

The Pipedrive integration logs every call you make or take in CallForges as a completed Call activity on the matching Pipedrive person, or as a note. It also lets you browse your Pipedrive people inside CallForges and import them as contacts to call.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 22 October 2026

## Before you start

- You need a CallForges owner or admin role to connect, configure or disconnect Pipedrive. Other users don't see the integration settings, but their calls are logged once they are mapped.

- Connect as a Pipedrive admin, so calls can be logged for every user in the company.

- One CallForges workspace connects to one Pipedrive company.

## Connect Pipedrive

- In CallForges, open Integrations and choose Pipedrive.

- Click Connect. Pipedrive opens in the same tab.

- Sign in to Pipedrive if asked, choose the company, review the permissions and click Allow and install.

- You come back to the Connection tab, which shows the Pipedrive company, who connected it and when.

If the Pipedrive company is already connected to another CallForges workspace, CallForges asks before moving it. That other workspace then stops logging calls to Pipedrive.

If Pipedrive later asks CallForges to sign in again (for example, after the app was uninstalled in Pipedrive), the Connection tab shows Reconnect. Calls made in the meantime wait and are sent once you reconnect.

Pipedrive before it is connected: click Connect.

The Connection tab after connecting Pipedrive.

## Map users

Calls are logged only for CallForges users who are matched to a Pipedrive user. That Pipedrive user becomes the owner of the Call activity. Open the Map users tab:

- Click Auto-map by e-mail to match every user whose e-mail address is the same in both products.

- For anyone left, choose their Pipedrive user from the list, or leave them on Not mapped.

- Click Save.

Calls by an unmapped user are skipped, and each skip shows up in Activity with the reason. Use Show unmapped only to find the users who still need a match. After you map them, you can send their skipped calls from Activity.

Map users: match each CallForges user to their Pipedrive user.

## Call logging settings

Open the Settings tab, change what you need and click Save changes.

### Workflow: what each call becomes

Choose separately for outbound answered calls, outbound unanswered calls, inbound answered calls, missed calls and voicemails:

Option | What is written in Pipedrive

Call activity | A completed activity of type Call on the person, with its duration, owner, outcome, the disposition and the call notes. It counts in Pipedrive's activity reports.

Note | A note on the person with the same details written as text.

Don't log | Nothing. The call is not written to Pipedrive.

### What each call activity includes

- Link to the recording adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the recording plays.

- Link to the transcript adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the transcript is read.

- AI summary adds the call's AI summary, when it has one. Summaries are made for English calls long enough to summarise, on plans that include them.

Recordings and transcripts stay in CallForges. They are not copied into Pipedrive, and only signed-in users of your CallForges workspace can open the links.

### Connected numbers

Leave Log calls on all numbers on to log calls on every number your workspace owns, including numbers bought later. Turn it off to pick the numbers to log. Calls on numbers that aren't picked are skipped.

### When calls are logged

A call is written to Pipedrive within a few minutes of ending, so the disposition and notes the user adds after the call are included. If the call is changed later, for example a new disposition, the same Call activity is updated.

Settings → Workflow: choose what each kind of call becomes in Pipedrive.

## The caller's name when a call rings

When someone who isn't in your CallForges Contacts calls one of your numbers, CallForges looks the number up in Pipedrive while the call rings, and the name appears on the ring card a moment later.

The ring never waits for the answer. If Pipedrive is slow or busy, or several people share the number, the card shows the number alone. A contact saved in CallForges always comes first. CallForges keeps the answer in memory for a few minutes and doesn't save it.

## Unknown numbers

CallForges finds the Pipedrive person by phone number, with or without the country code. In Settings → General:

- Create a Pipedrive person if the number isn't found: when no person in Pipedrive has the number, CallForges creates one so the call is still logged. When this is off, the call isn't logged and Activity shows that the person wasn't found.

- Use the phone number as the new person's name: used when CallForges has no name for the caller. When this is off, the new person is named "Unknown caller". This applies only while creating people is on.

- Add Pipedrive people to CallForges Contacts: when a call reaches someone who is in Pipedrive but not in your CallForges Contacts, CallForges adds them to Contacts and links the two. Off by default.

Settings → General: unknown numbers, Contacts and what each entry includes.

## Import contacts

The Contacts tab lists the people in your Pipedrive company who have a phone number, read live from Pipedrive. Each row shows the person's organization and whether they are already in CallForges, with a link to open them in Pipedrive.

- Search, or filter by one of your saved Pipedrive people filters with All lists.

- Select people, or import everyone in the chosen filter.

- Click Import and choose an existing CallForges list or name a new one.

Imported people become CallForges contacts linked to their Pipedrive records, ready to call from a campaign or the dialer. Click Sync now to bring in later changes. CallForges doesn't copy your Pipedrive data on a schedule; it reads Pipedrive only when you open the tab, import or sync.

The Contacts tab: your Pipedrive people with a phone number, ready to import.

## Log past calls

Connecting logs the calls that happen from then on. To send calls your workspace made before you connected, use Settings → Log past calls:

- Under How far back, pick a date range. It reaches back up to 1 year.

- Click Log past calls. CallForges counts the calls first and shows how many would be logged, and which users' calls would be skipped because they aren't mapped.

- Confirm. A progress bar shows the calls being sent.

Past calls are sent in the background and never delay the logging of new calls. To stop a run, open Activity, go to the Queued tab and click Stop queued.

Log past calls: pick how far back, then confirm.

## Activity

The Activity tab lists every call and what happened to it in Pipedrive: logged (and whether as a Call activity or a note), queued, failed or skipped, with the reason. You can retry one call, or use Retry all for every failed or skipped call that matches your filters. Never logged lists calls that were never sent to Pipedrive.

If Pipedrive can't be reached or its API limit is used up, CallForges pauses and shows how many calls are waiting. They are sent automatically once Pipedrive accepts requests again. Nothing is lost.

Activity: what happened to each call in Pipedrive.

## Disconnect

- Open Integrations → Pipedrive.

- Click Disconnect and confirm.

Calls stop being logged to Pipedrive and the user mapping is cleared. CallForges gives up its access to your Pipedrive company. Call activities and notes already written stay in Pipedrive, and your logging settings are kept in case you reconnect. You can also uninstall the app from Pipedrive (Tools and apps → Marketplace apps) at any time; CallForges then shows Reconnect.

The Disconnect confirmation.

## What CallForges can access

When you connect, CallForges asks Pipedrive for these permissions on your company:

Permission | Why

`base` | Connect the app, and read your user, company and saved filters.

`contacts:full` | Find the person by phone number, list people in the Contacts tab, create a person for an unknown number when you turn that on, and write notes on people.

`activities:full` | Write each call as a Call activity, and update it when the call changes.

`users:read` | List Pipedrive users for Map users and Auto-map by e-mail, and set the owner of each Call activity.

`phone-integration` | Pipedrive's permission for calling apps. CallForges writes calls as Call activities today and doesn't write Pipedrive call logs.

Your Pipedrive access is stored encrypted and used only for the features above. See our Privacy Policy.
