# HighLevel integration

The HighLevel integration logs every call you make or take in CallForges on the matching contact in a HighLevel sub-account. The call goes into the contact's conversation with a note holding its details, or is written as a note alone. It also lets you browse your HighLevel contacts inside CallForges and import them as contacts to call.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 22 November 2026

## Before you start

- You need a CallForges owner or admin role to connect, configure or disconnect HighLevel. Other users don't see the integration settings, but their calls are logged once they are mapped.

- You need a HighLevel login that can open the sub-account you want to connect.

- One CallForges workspace connects to one HighLevel sub-account (also called a business account). An agency with several sub-accounts connects each one from its own CallForges workspace.

## Connect HighLevel

Connect from CallForges with the steps below, or find CallForges in the HighLevel Marketplace: CallForges in the HighLevel Marketplace.

- In CallForges, open Integrations and choose HighLevel.

- Click Connect, then Continue to HighLevel. HighLevel opens.

- Sign in to HighLevel if asked, choose the sub-account and approve the permissions.

- You come back to the Connection tab, which shows the sub-account, who connected it and when.

If the sub-account is already connected to another CallForges workspace, CallForges asks before moving it. That other workspace then stops logging calls to HighLevel. If you connect a different sub-account to this workspace, CallForges asks you to confirm the switch.

If HighLevel later asks CallForges to sign in again (for example, after the app was uninstalled in HighLevel), the Connection tab shows Reconnect. Calls made in the meantime wait and are sent once you reconnect.

HighLevel before it is connected: click Connect.

The Connection tab after connecting HighLevel.

## Agency logins and installs from HighLevel

### If you sign in with an agency login

CallForges asks which sub-account to connect. Pick one under Sub-account, searching by name if the list is long, and click Connect. Only that sub-account is connected, never the rest of the agency.

Choosing the sub-account after an agency login.

### If you start the install from HighLevel

CallForges is listed in the HighLevel Marketplace: CallForges in the HighLevel Marketplace. With an agency login, install from Agency View:

- Click Install, then Proceed to Install.

- At Select Sub-Account, choose the sub-account and click Continue.

- Click Allow & install.

The Install button in Sub-Account View does nothing. The agency also needs at least one sub-account first: without one, Proceed to Install does nothing.

HighLevel then sends you to CallForges. Sign in if asked. CallForges shows what is about to be connected: the HighLevel sub-account and the CallForges workspace you have open.

- Nothing is connected until you click Connect.

- If you belong to several workspaces, click Switch to connect a different one.

- Cancel connects nothing. You can start again from Integrations.

The confirm step: check the sub-account and the workspace, then click Connect.

## Map users

Calls are logged only for CallForges users who are matched to a HighLevel user. Open the Map users tab:

- Click Auto-map by e-mail to match every user whose e-mail address is the same in both products.

- For anyone left, choose their HighLevel user from the list, or leave them on Not mapped.

- Click Save mappings.

Calls by an unmapped user are skipped, and each skip shows up in Activity with the reason. Use Show unmapped only to find the users who still need a match. After you map them, you can send their skipped calls from Activity.

Map users: match each CallForges user to their HighLevel user.

## Call logging settings

Open the Settings tab, change what you need and click Save changes.

### Workflow: what each call becomes

Choose separately for outbound answered calls, outbound unanswered calls, inbound answered calls, missed calls and voicemails:

Option | What is written in HighLevel

Call activity | The call is added to the contact's conversation, with a note holding its time, duration, outcome, disposition and call notes. The contact is tagged with the disposition and the call's outcome. If HighLevel refuses the conversation entry, the call is still saved as a note on the contact.

Note | A note on the contact with the same details written as text. Nothing is added to the conversation, and no tag is added.

Don't log | Nothing. The call is not written to HighLevel.

The call itself happens in CallForges, so these calls may not appear in HighLevel's own call reports.

### Disposition tags

With Call activity, a call that has a disposition tags the contact with it. If the disposition changes later, CallForges replaces the tag it added with the new one. If the disposition is cleared, CallForges removes the tag it added.

CallForges only ever removes a tag it added itself. A tag the contact already had, and every other tag on the contact, is never touched.

### What each logged call includes

- Link to the recording adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the recording plays.

- Link to the transcript adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the transcript is read.

- AI summary adds the call's AI summary, when it has one. Summaries are made for English calls long enough to summarise, on plans that include them.

- Save the recording in HighLevel attaches the recording to the call's entry in the conversation. It's off by default and works only while Secured recording links is off in Settings → Call settings. The attachment uses a share link that stops working after a time; the link to the call's page keeps working.

Transcripts stay in CallForges, and so do recordings unless you turn on Save the recording in HighLevel. Only signed-in users of your CallForges workspace can open the links.

### Connected numbers

Leave Log calls on all numbers on to log calls on every number your workspace owns, including numbers bought later. Turn it off to pick the numbers to log. Calls on numbers that aren't picked are skipped.

### When calls are logged

A call is written to HighLevel within a few minutes of ending, so the disposition and notes the user adds after the call are included. If the call is changed later, for example a new disposition, the same note is updated. The entry in the conversation stays as it was.

Settings → Workflow: choose what each kind of call becomes in HighLevel.

## Outcome tags

With Call activity, every logged call tags the contact with its outcome: `callforges-answered`, `callforges-no-answer`, `callforges-missed`, `callforges-busy`, `callforges-failed`, `callforges-cancelled` or `callforges-voicemail`. Use these tags to start a HighLevel workflow, for example a text after a missed call.

CallForges never takes an outcome tag away for good, so a contact can hold several. If the contact already holds the tag from an earlier call, CallForges removes it and adds it again for the new call.

## Follow-up tasks and the last outcome

Turn these on in Settings. Both are off by default.

- Add a follow-up task on a missed call: each missed call or voicemail logged as Call activity gets one task to call back, due a day later and assigned to the mapped HighLevel user.

- Save the last outcome on the contact: each call logged as Call activity fills a Last call outcome field on the contact with its outcome. CallForges creates the field the first time it needs it.

Connections made before this feature need to reconnect to fill the field. The call is logged either way.

## The caller's name when a call rings

When someone who isn't in your CallForges Contacts calls one of your numbers, CallForges looks the number up in HighLevel while the call rings, and the name appears on the ring card a moment later.

The ring never waits for the answer. If HighLevel is slow or busy, or several contacts share the number, the card shows the number alone. A contact saved in CallForges always comes first. CallForges keeps the answer in memory for a few minutes and doesn't save it.

## Unknown numbers

CallForges finds the HighLevel contact by phone number, including a contact's additional phone numbers. In Settings → General:

- Create a HighLevel contact if the number isn't found: when no contact in HighLevel has the number, CallForges creates one so the call is still logged. This is on by default. When it is off, the call isn't logged and Activity shows that the contact wasn't found.

- Use the phone number as the new contact's name: used when CallForges has no name for the caller. When this is off, the new contact is named "Unknown caller". This applies only while creating contacts is on.

- Add HighLevel contacts to CallForges Contacts: when a call reaches someone who is in HighLevel but not in your CallForges Contacts, CallForges adds them to Contacts and links the two. Off by default.

If HighLevel refuses a new contact, for example because the sub-account doesn't allow duplicates, Activity shows the reason.

Settings → General: unknown numbers, Contacts and what each entry includes.

## Import contacts

The Contacts tab lists the contacts in your HighLevel sub-account who have a phone number, read live from HighLevel. Each row shows the contact's company and whether they are already in CallForges.

- Search, or filter by a HighLevel tag with All lists. Smart Lists aren't available here.

- Select contacts, or import everyone in the chosen tag.

- Click Import selected or Import all, and choose an existing CallForges list or name a new one.

Imported contacts become CallForges contacts linked to their HighLevel records, ready to call from a campaign or the dialer. Click Sync now to bring in later changes. CallForges doesn't copy your HighLevel data on a schedule; it reads HighLevel only when you open the tab, import or sync.

The Contacts tab: your HighLevel contacts with a phone number, ready to import.

## Log past calls

Connecting logs the calls that happen from then on. To send calls your workspace made before you connected, use Settings → Log past calls:

- Under How far back, pick a date range. It reaches back up to 1 year.

- Click Log past calls. CallForges counts the calls first and shows how many would be logged, and which users' calls would be skipped because they aren't mapped.

- Confirm. A progress bar shows the calls being sent.

Past calls are sent in the background and never delay the logging of new calls. To stop a run, open Activity, go to the Queued tab and click Stop queued.

Log past calls: pick how far back, then confirm.

## Activity

The Activity tab lists every call and what happened to it in HighLevel: logged, queued, failed or skipped, with the reason. You can retry one call, or use Retry all for every failed or skipped call that matches your filters. Never logged lists calls that were never sent to HighLevel.

If HighLevel's limits are reached or HighLevel can't be reached, CallForges pauses and sends the waiting calls once HighLevel accepts requests again. Nothing is lost.

If HighLevel says the sub-account isn't active, the page shows Paused — account inactive. CallForges keeps retrying by itself and you don't need to reconnect. Nothing is lost.

Activity: what happened to each call in HighLevel.

## Disconnect

- Open Integrations → HighLevel.

- Click Disconnect and confirm.

Calls stop being logged to HighLevel and the user mapping is cleared. CallForges uninstalls itself from this sub-account only, never from the agency or its other sub-accounts. Call logs already written stay in HighLevel, and your logging settings are kept in case you reconnect.

If HighLevel doesn't confirm the removal, CallForges shows Disconnected here, but HighLevel did not confirm it and asks you to remove CallForges' access in HighLevel's settings too.

You can also uninstall the app from HighLevel at any time. CallForges then shows Reconnect.

The Disconnect confirmation.

## What CallForges can access

When you connect, CallForges asks HighLevel for these permissions on your sub-account:

Permission | Why

`contacts.readonly` | Find the contact by phone number and list contacts in the Contacts tab.

`contacts.write` | Write notes and tags on contacts, and create a contact for an unknown number when that setting is on.

`conversations.readonly`, `conversations.write`, `conversations/message.write` | Add the call to the contact's conversation.

`users.readonly` | List HighLevel users for Map users and Auto-map by e-mail.

`locations.readonly` | Identify the sub-account you connected.

`locations/tags.readonly` | Show your tags in the Contacts tab's filter.

`locations/customFields.readonly`, `locations/customFields.write` | Create and fill the Last call outcome field.

`oauth.write` | Remove CallForges from the sub-account when you disconnect, and connect the sub-account you pick after an agency login.

`oauth.readonly` | List an agency's sub-accounts so you can pick one.

Your HighLevel access is stored encrypted and used only for the features above. See our Privacy Policy.

URL: https://callforges.com/help/articles/clio-integration

# Clio integration

The Clio integration logs every call you make or take in CallForges as a phone call in Clio Manage, on the matching contact and on their matter when they have exactly one open matter. If you turn it on, it also adds a time entry for each call with talk time.

Written by CallForges Support · Updated 7 November 2026

## Before you start

- You need a CallForges owner or admin role to connect, configure or disconnect Clio. Other users don't see the integration settings, but their calls are logged once they are mapped.

- Connect with a Clio administrator. If Clio's Contacts Visibility hides contacts from the user who connects, CallForges can't find those contacts.

- The integration works with Clio Manage. Someone who exists only in Clio Grow counts as an unknown number.

- Clio is offered for accounts in the United States, the ones you sign in to at app.clio.com.

- Your Clio plan needs to allow third-party apps. If Clio refuses the connection, check your plan with Clio.

- One CallForges workspace connects to one Clio account.

## Connect Clio

- In CallForges, open Integrations and choose Clio.

- Click Connect.

- Under Where is your Clio account?, choose United States and click Continue to Clio.

- Sign in to Clio if asked and allow access.

- You come back to the Connection tab, which shows the Clio account, who connected it and when.

If the Clio account is already connected to another CallForges workspace, CallForges asks before moving it. That other workspace then stops logging calls to Clio.

If Clio later asks CallForges to sign in again, the Connection tab shows Reconnect. Calls made in the meantime wait and are sent once you reconnect.

Clio before it is connected: click Connect.

Choose where your Clio account lives, then continue to Clio.

The Connection tab after connecting Clio.

## Map users

Calls are logged only for CallForges users who are matched to a Clio user. Open the Map users tab:

- Click Auto-map by e-mail to match every user whose e-mail address is the same in both products.

- For anyone left, choose their Clio user from the list, or leave them on Not mapped.

- Click Save mappings.

Calls by an unmapped user are skipped, and each skip shows up in Activity with the reason. Use Show unmapped only to find the users who still need a match. After you map them, you can send their skipped calls from Activity.

Map users: match each CallForges user to their Clio user.

## Call logging settings

Open the Settings tab, change what you need and click Save changes.

### Workflow: what each call becomes

Choose separately for outbound answered calls, outbound unanswered calls, inbound answered calls, missed calls and voicemails:

Option | What is written in Clio

Call activity | A phone call on the contact, with the call's details in its body.

Don't log | Nothing. The call is not written to Clio.

Note isn't available for Clio. Every logged call is saved as a phone call, because Clio can only link a time entry to a phone call.

### Which matter a call goes on

The phone call is linked to a matter only when the contact has exactly one open matter. With no open matter, or more than one, it stays on the contact alone. To put a call on a matter afterward, click Move to a matter on that call.

### What each phone call includes

- Link to the recording adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the recording plays.

- Link to the transcript adds a link to the call's page in CallForges, where the transcript is read.

- AI summary adds the call's AI summary, when it has one. Summaries are made for English calls long enough to summarise, on plans that include them.

- Add a time entry for each call is explained under Time entries.

- Save the recording in Clio stores the recording in the matter's documents, or the contact's when the call has no matter. It's off by default and works only while Secured recording links is off in Settings → Call settings. A call on no contact stores nothing.

Transcripts stay in CallForges, and so do recordings unless you turn on Save the recording in Clio. Only signed-in users of your CallForges workspace can open the links.

### Connected numbers

Leave Log calls on all numbers on to log calls on every number your workspace owns, including numbers bought later. Turn it off to pick the numbers to log. Calls on numbers that aren't picked are skipped.

### When calls are logged

A call is written to Clio within a few minutes of ending, so the disposition and notes the user adds after the call are included. If the call is changed later, for example a new disposition, the same phone call is updated.

A phone call you delete in Clio stays deleted. CallForges doesn't write a new one, and Activity says so.

Settings → Workflow: choose what each kind of call becomes in Clio.

## Time entries

CallForges can add a Clio time entry for each call. This is a setting on your Clio connection and it is off by default. To turn it on, open Settings, go to What each phone call includes, turn on Add a time entry for each call and click Save changes.

Add a time entry for each call is off until you turn it on.

While it is on:

- Each call with talk time gets one time entry. A call with no talk time gets none.

- Time entries are non-billable by default. Turn on Make time entries billable to change that.

- In Map users, the Time entries switch turns them off for one user.

- The time entry is linked to the phone call, and to the matter when the phone call has one.

- It is dated in the mapped user's Clio time zone.

- A later edit updates the phone call and leaves the time entry alone, except Move to a matter, which moves both.

- A time entry you delete in Clio isn't added back.

Turning the setting on writes nothing by itself for calls already in Clio. One of those calls gets a time entry the next time it is sent to Clio, for example after an edit, if it had talk time. Calls you send with Log past calls while it is on get one too, if they had talk time. Turning it off removes nothing: time entries already written stay in Clio.

## Unknown numbers

CallForges finds the Clio contact by phone number, trying the number in several formats.

A call to a number that is on no contact is still logged. Clio keeps it under Inbox → Logs, on no contact and no matter. CallForges doesn't create a contact by default. To add one after the call, click Add to Clio on that call. To create one automatically, use Settings → General:

- Create a Clio contact if the number isn't found: when no contact in Clio has the number, CallForges creates one and logs the call on it. Off by default.

- Use the phone number as the new contact's name: used when CallForges has no name for the caller. When this is off, the new contact is named "Unknown caller". This applies only while creating contacts is on.

Settings → General: unknown numbers, Contacts and what each entry includes.

## Add to Clio and Move to a matter

Both actions are on the call's page and on its row in Activity, for anyone who can log that call.

- Add to Clio shows on a call logged with no contact. Fill in the name and CallForges creates the contact with the call's number and links the call to it. If a Clio contact already has that number, the call is linked to it. If several do, nothing changes and you link the call in Clio.

- Move to a matter shows on a call with a contact and no matter. Pick one of the contact's open matters, and the phone call and its time entry move there. If Clio keeps the time entry where it is, for example because it was billed, only the phone call moves and CallForges says so. You need to be mapped to a Clio user to see matters.

## The caller's name when a call rings

When someone who isn't in your CallForges Contacts calls one of your numbers, CallForges looks the number up in Clio while the call rings, and the name appears on the ring card a moment later.

The ring never waits for the answer. If Clio is slow or busy, or several contacts share the number, the card shows the number alone. A contact saved in CallForges always comes first. CallForges keeps the answer in memory for a few minutes and doesn't save it.

Users mapped to a Clio user also see the caller's open matters. Clio allows fewer requests per second than other CRMs, so its name can take a few seconds to appear.

## Contacts

The Contacts tab lists the contacts in your Clio account who have a phone number, read live from Clio, with a link to open each one in Clio.

Clio contacts can't be imported into CallForges, so they stay in Clio. The import buttons and Sync now are greyed out for Clio, and so is Add Clio contacts to CallForges Contacts in Settings. Clio has no contact lists, so All lists is greyed out too.

The Contacts tab: your Clio contacts with a phone number, which stay in Clio.

## Log past calls

Connecting logs the calls that happen from then on. To send calls your workspace made before you connected, use Settings → Log past calls:

- Under How far back, pick a date range. It reaches back up to 1 year.

- Click Log past calls. CallForges counts the calls first and shows how many would be logged, and which users' calls would be skipped because they aren't mapped.

- Confirm. A progress bar shows the calls being sent.

Past calls are sent in the background and never delay the logging of new calls. To stop a run, open Activity, go to the Queued tab and click Stop queued.

Log past calls: pick how far back, then confirm.

## Activity

The Activity tab lists every call and what happened to it in Clio: logged, queued, failed or skipped, with the reason. You can retry one call, or use Retry all for every failed or skipped call that matches your filters. Never logged lists calls that were never sent to Clio.

Clio limits how many requests an app can make. After a burst of calls, some phone calls may appear in Clio a little late. Nothing is lost.

Activity: what happened to each call in Clio.

## Disconnect

- Open Integrations → Clio.

- Click Disconnect and confirm.

Calls stop being logged to Clio and the user mapping is cleared. CallForges gives up its access to your Clio account and forgets the Clio names and e-mail addresses it held. Phone calls and time entries already written stay in Clio, and your logging settings are kept in case you reconnect.

If Clio doesn't confirm the removal, CallForges shows Disconnected here, but Clio did not confirm it and asks you to remove CallForges' access in Clio's settings too.

You can also remove CallForges in Clio, under My Integrations, at any time. CallForges then shows Not connected or Reconnect.

The Disconnect confirmation.

## What CallForges can access

When you connect, CallForges asks Clio for these permissions on your account:

Permission | Why

Contacts (read and write) | Find the contact by phone number, list contacts in the Contacts tab, and create a contact for an unknown number when you turn that on.

Communications (read and write) | Write and update the phone calls.

Activities (read and write) | Add time entries when you turn them on.

Matters (read) | Find the contact's open matters.

Documents (read and write) | Save the recording in Clio when you turn that on.

Users (read) | List Clio users for Map users and Auto-map by e-mail, and read each user's time zone.

CallForges doesn't ask for your Clio notes or calendars. Connections made before recordings could be saved need to reconnect to use that switch; calls are logged either way.

Your Clio access is stored encrypted and used only for the features above. See our Security page and Privacy Policy.
